updates.detail: The challengers to SB 253 and SB 261 filed a second supplemental-authority letter with the Ninth Circuit on November 3, 2026, attaching two recent judicial decisions and arguing they confirm an entitlement to preliminary relief before the November 10 reporting deadline. A letter of this kind is not a motion and seeks no new relief; the court has not ruled, and the Ninth Circuit's published listing of opinions and orders was current through November 6, 2026 with the case absent, leaving it roughly ten months submitted after argument on January 9, 2026. CARB has published no extension, no change in enforcement posture, no new template and no deadline-eve guidance, and its most recent bulletin remains the October 12, 2026 notice that the regulation took effect. CARB has also published no response to the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency's October 29, 2026 request to exempt national banks, and the OCC itself took no further action even though its news releases run through November 4, 2026 — so the silence on both sides is documented, not merely unobserved.
updates.so_what: File by November 10 as planned, including if you are a national bank: the only order in force still denies relief as to SB 253, and no request, letter or pending appeal has suspended the deadline.
updates.headline: With one day to go, California's first emissions reporting deadline stands — no court ruling, no extension, no answer to the federal banking regulator
updates.source_title: US Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit — Opinions (listing current through November 6, 2026; No. 25-5327 absent)

updates.detail: SBTi published two standard operating procedures on October 30, 2026, both approved by its Technical Council, adopted by its Board of Trustees and effective on publication: Version 2.0 of the procedure for developing and revising SBTi standards, and a new Version 1.0 procedure for methods, metrics and pathways. Version 2.0 creates a new instrument called a sector specification, which adds to, supersedes or modifies requirements of the Corporate Net-Zero Standard for one sector, is not a standalone standard and does not require Board adoption. It also makes the claims a validated company may make a mandatory component of every standard, and requires each new version to state its publication date, its effective date and a transition period. The methods procedure sets one new deadline: the eligibility criteria for recognising third-party pathways are to be made public by the end of Q4 2026, with the recognition process implemented in 2027.
updates.so_what: Nothing to file, but note that SBTi can now add sector-specific requirements to V2.0 without Board adoption, so new sector obligations can arrive with less notice than a standalone standard would have given.
updates.headline: SBTi rewrites how it makes standards, and creates a lighter route for sector rules
updates.source_title: New Standard Operating Procedures to deliver agility while reinforcing governance

updates.detail: The ISSB Update covering the October 29, 2026 meeting published during the week of November 2, 2026, resolving what the board made of its staff's recommendations. The board took three tentative decisions: that the SASB Standards will explain that IFRS S1 requirements apply when they are used to prepare disclosures under the ISSB's standards (agreed 10 of 10); that the IFRS S1 paragraph 73 reliefs will be available in that context, covering information whose disclosure is prohibited by law and commercially sensitive information about a sustainability-related opportunity (9 of 10); and that the proportionality mechanism — reasonable and supportable information available without undue cost or effort — will also apply (9 of 10). The staff proposal to rename the SASB Standards was discussed but the board was not asked to decide, so it remains open, as do whether an additional proportionality mechanism should apply to particular SASB metrics and whether the same measures apply when the SASB Standards are used on their own. All three decisions are tentative and subject to formal ballot under the ISSB's due process.
updates.so_what: Where SASB metrics feed disclosure made under the ISSB standards, you can now plan on the same relief and proportionality architecture that applies to the rest of IFRS S1 rather than a stricter parallel regime — but do not yet rewrite internal references to the SASB Standards, because the rename is still live.
updates.headline: ISSB extends its relief and proportionality rules to the SASB Standards; the proposed rename is still undecided

updates.detail: The OCC, the federal regulator that charters and supervises national banks, wrote to CARB on October 29, 2026 asking it to exempt federally chartered banks from California's two climate disclosure laws, SB 253 and SB 261, or to confirm that those banks need not comply. The letter argues the laws may conflict with federal preemption and with the rules reserving supervision of national banks to federal regulators, and raises Supremacy Clause, safety-and-soundness and competitive-harm concerns. It is a request, not a rule or a preemption determination, and carries no legal effect on its own: it asks for no delay and does not mention the November 10, 2026 reporting deadline, which stands. CARB has published no response, and the OCC says it will continue to monitor state law and act where appropriate.
updates.so_what: Keep filing to November 10 - nothing has changed - but national banks should watch for a CARB answer, and everyone else should read this as a second front opening against California alongside the undecided Ninth Circuit appeal.
updates.headline: A federal banking regulator asks California to excuse national banks from its climate reporting laws
updates.source_title: OCC Raises Concerns with California's Climate Disclosure Laws (News Release NR 2026-95)

updates.detail: Member states' permanent representatives endorsed the final compromise text amending the EU Emissions Trading System market stability reserve on October 28, 2026, and the Presidency sent the agreed text to the chair of the European Parliament's environment committee. The Council document is the first primary confirmation of the figures reported a week earlier: allowances held in the reserve above 400 million stop being valid up to the day before the amending decision enters into force, after which the threshold becomes 700 million. This is a procedural endorsement rather than adoption - a committee vote, a Parliament first reading, formal Council adoption and publication in the Official Journal all remain. It concerns the main EU ETS reserve and is a different file from the separate ETS2 reserve amendment covering buildings and road transport.
updates.so_what: A carbon-price input, not a disclosure duty - feed it into EU ETS cost forecasts for the late 2030s and otherwise ignore it.
updates.headline: Member states sign off on the deal to keep cancelling surplus EU carbon allowances
updates.source_title: Council of the European Union, document 14944/26 - Outcome of Proceedings, 28 October 2026

updates.detail: Minutes of the Corporate Standard technical working group's eleventh full meeting, held October 27, 2026 and published on GHG Protocol's governance repository in early November, record the secretariat stating that neither the working group nor the Independent Standards Board supports requiring verification, leaving a recommendation, an option, or silence as the live choices. ISO's representative argued that verification should be mandatory, and the minutes note that the reporting clause in the second working draft of ISO 14064-1 is conditional on verification having been obtained — so the two documents being merged currently point in opposite directions. Some members argued GHG Protocol should not settle the assurance question at all because it reaches into legal and regulatory territory. The item was shortened and no votes were taken, so nothing is decided; the working group's feedback survey closes November 13, 2026 and the next full meeting is November 24, 2026.
updates.so_what: Plan assurance scope on the basis that the merged standard will probably not mandate verification, while remembering that your binding assurance requirements come from elsewhere — California from 2027, the EU, and SBTi for Category A companies — not from GHG Protocol.
updates.headline: The merged corporate standard looks unlikely to require third-party verification — and ISO disagrees
updates.source_title: GHG Protocol — Corporate Standard Full TWG Meeting 11 minutes (October 27, 2026)

updates.detail: CARB staff gave the Board an informational update on SB 253 implementation on October 22, 2026 and spent substantial time on Scope 3. Staff said they will hold a further public workshop before issuing a staff report and a draft regulation for the 2027 cycle, so the formal 45-day notice has not started. CARB confirmed that fee notices go out from December 10, 2026 with payment due within 60 days. Staff also said CARB aims to publish the outcomes of the 2026 reporting cycle within 90 days after November 10.
updates.so_what: Do not wait for the 2027 Scope 3 rule before building supplier, travel, commuting and waste data flows - the rule is still months from a formal proposal, but the categories are already signposted.
updates.headline: CARB briefs its Board on SB 253 and signals the 2027 Scope 3 rulemaking is still some way off
updates.source_title: California SB 253 Corporate Climate Reporting Deadline 2026 (Bass Berry, October 29, 2026)

updates.detail: The ISSB published its exposure draft on nature-related disclosures on October 22, 2026, opening a 120-day consultation that closes February 19, 2027. The proposals take the form of a Practice Statement, and the ISSB states that a company is not required to comply with a Practice Statement in order to state compliance with ISSB Standards. The ISSB is also asking respondents whether the content should instead be finalised as a full standard, so the instrument itself is still an open question. The draft leaves IFRS S1 and IFRS S2 unchanged and sets no Scope 1, Scope 2 or Scope 3 requirements.
updates.so_what: Nothing in your emissions inventory changes - treat this as a voluntary framework worth commenting on, not a new accounting obligation.
updates.headline: The ISSB publishes its nature reporting proposals - and they are voluntary by design
updates.source_title: ISSB consults on its proposals for nature-related disclosures (IFRS Foundation)

updates.detail: Council and Parliament negotiators reached a provisional agreement on October 20, 2026, announced by the Council the following day, on a targeted amendment to the market stability reserve of the main EU emissions trading system. The threshold above which surplus allowances are permanently cancelled rises from 400 million to 700 million allowances, so far fewer allowances will be invalidated. The co-legislators kept the invalidation mechanism in place rather than halting it indefinitely as the Commission had proposed. The higher threshold takes immediate effect once both institutions endorse and formally adopt the text.
updates.so_what: No reporting change - this affects the EU carbon price you pay, not what you disclose, and it is a separate file from the ETS2 reserve amendment the Council signed off on October 9.
updates.headline: EU negotiators agree to keep cancelling surplus carbon allowances, at a far higher threshold
updates.source_title: ETS market stability reserve: Council and Parliament reach provisional agreement on targeted amendment (Council of the EU)

updates.detail: Parliament and Council negotiators held their first political negotiation on extending CBAM to downstream goods on October 20, 2026, setting out their mandates without hitting a blocking issue. The three positions remain far apart on scope, reported as 180 additional product categories from the Commission, 400 from the Council and 457 from Parliament. Negotiators agreed to continue technical work on a de minimis threshold for aluminium products, the treatment of metal waste, whether online platforms fall in scope, and how default values are set globally. No provisional agreement was reached and the next negotiating meeting is set for November 30, 2026; neither institution has published a readout, so the meeting is reported by EU trade press only.
updates.so_what: If you import goods into the EU, the scope that decides your exposure is still unsettled - size the risk against the 457-category upper bound rather than the Commission 180.
updates.headline: Talks open on widening the EU carbon border tax, with the product count still hundreds apart
updates.source_title: First talks between European Parliament and EU Council on extending CBAM raise no major issues (Agence Europe, Bulletin 13965) - trade press, no institutional readout

updates.detail: The ISB has settled on building two market-based methods rather than choosing between them. Method 1 would add hourly matching, deliverability and incrementality requirements; Method 2 keeps the 2015 Scope 2 Guidance requirements, so existing procurement strategies continue to work. The ISB's direction of travel is that companies may report under Method 2 and should report under Method 1 until a date still to be determined, shall disclose which method they applied before that date, and shall report under Method 1 after it where data meeting the quality criteria is available. Whether either method ends up optional or required is explicitly still open, every date is unset, and a TWG workshop on deliverability, incrementality, feasibility and implementation timing is set for later in October 2026.
updates.so_what: Do not retire annual-matching procurement on the assumption hourly matching is coming; plan instead for a disclosed choice between two methods, and treat hourly data collection as an option to keep open rather than a commitment.
updates.headline: GHG Protocol will offer two ways to count purchased electricity, not one
updates.source_title: GHG Protocol: Scope 2 Market-based Method Update - From 2025-2026 Public Consultation to Current Status

updates.detail: EFRAG opened a Request for Input on its sustainability reporting agenda for 2027 to 2029, saying the core CSRD standard-setting milestones are nearing completion. It seeks views on the balance of its activities, the shape of future implementation support and digital tools, and research priorities for emerging topics. Responses are due February 15, 2027, and EFRAG expects to issue the final workplan in the second quarter of 2027, subject to approval by the EFRAG Sustainability Reporting Board. EFRAG explicitly encourages stakeholders from outside the EU to take part, tying that to implementation support for ESRS 40a and interoperability.
updates.so_what: If ESRS 40a will apply to you as a non-EU parent, this is the window to ask for the implementation guidance and interoperability tools you will need - none exist yet for the revised standards.
updates.headline: EFRAG asks what reporting support it should build after 2027
updates.source_title: EFRAG Launches Public Consultation on Its Sustainability Reporting Agenda for 2027-2029

updates.detail: EPA published an interim final rule on October 14, 2026 (91 FR 65112) moving the reporting-year 2025 deadline under the Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program from October 30, 2026 to March 10, 2027. The rule took effect on publication, so the October deadline no longer applies. EPA cited the volume of comments on its September 2025 proposal to end the program for most source categories and the need for more time. Comments on the extension itself are due November 30, 2026, and the proposal to rescind the program remains unfinalised.
updates.so_what: Rebaseline your facility-level reporting calendar to March 10, 2027, and keep preparing the data - the program is still in force and only the deadline moved.
updates.headline: EPA pushes the 2025-data reporting deadline to March 10, 2027
updates.source_title: Extending the Reporting Deadline Under the Greenhouse Gas Reporting Rule for Reporting Year 2025 (91 FR 65112)

updates.detail: OAL approved CARB's initial California Corporate Greenhouse Gas Reporting and Climate-Related Financial Risk Disclosure Regulation on October 12, 2026, and CARB states the effective date is the same day. The regulation is codified at Title 17 of the California Code of Regulations, Article 6, sections 96070 to 96077. CARB confirms the 2026 emissions reporting deadline is November 10, 2026, and that the first annual disclosures cover Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions only. Because the regulation took effect on filing rather than on California's default quarterly schedule, the effective date did not slip to January 1, 2027, which would have fallen after the deadline.
updates.so_what: Treat November 10 as a firm deadline set by a regulation now in force and file on it - the procedural uncertainty that justified holding back is gone.
updates.headline: California's emissions reporting rule is approved and in force, fixing November 10
updates.source_title: CARB: Initial Regulation Approved by the Office of Administrative Law (October 12, 2026)

updates.detail: CARB resubmitted the regulation to OAL on September 21, 2026 as file 2026-0921-06, and it was still on OAL's daily-updated under-review list 40 days later, with nothing filed with the Secretary of State. The open question was the effective date: California's default quarterly schedule would have delayed the rule to January 1, 2027, after the November 10 reporting deadline, unless it could take effect on filing. OAL approved the file later the same day and CARB states the regulation took effect immediately, so that gap never opened.
updates.so_what: Resolved the same day - see the approval item above; the November 10 deadline now rests on a regulation in force, not a pending file.
updates.headline: California's rule spent 40 days in legal review before clearing it
updates.source_title: Office of Administrative Law: Proposed Regulations Under Review (file 2026-0921-06)

updates.detail: EFRAG moved the deadline for its ESRS 40a cost-benefit survey from October 11 to October 18, 2026, saying the extension allows broader participation from the non-EU companies in scope. The survey is separate from, and closes before, the public consultation on the ESRS 40a exposure draft, which still closes October 31, 2026. Evidence from the survey feeds EFRAG's technical advice to the European Commission, which determines how heavy the final obligation on non-EU parents will be. Article 40a reporting applies to financial years beginning on or after January 1, 2028, with the first statements published in 2029.
updates.so_what: If a US-headquartered group will report under Article 40a, answer the cost survey by October 18 and the exposure draft consultation by October 31 — these are the last formal windows to influence the burden.
updates.headline: EFRAG extends its cost survey on the non-EU parent reporting standard to October 18
updates.source_title: EFRAG Extends Deadline for Cost-Benefit Analysis Survey on ESRS-40a to 18 October 2026

updates.detail: On October 9, 2026 the Council of the EU adopted an amendment to the market stability reserve for ETS2, the emissions trading system that will cover fuels burned in buildings and road transport from 2028. The amendment extends the reserve beyond 2030 and doubles the volume of allowances released when carbon costs exceed EUR 45 per tonne of CO2 equivalent in 2020 prices, from 20 million to 40 million. It also makes releases more gradual once allowances in circulation fall below 260 million. The act will be signed and published in the Official Journal and enters into force 20 days after publication, ahead of the 2028 launch.
updates.so_what: This is a cost exposure, not a reporting duty — factor a more firmly price-capped ETS2 into 2028 budgets for EU buildings, fleets and logistics.
updates.headline: The Council of the EU signs off on tighter supply controls for the EU's second carbon market
updates.source_title: ETS2: Council signs off on rules strengthening the market stability reserve

updates.detail: SBTi announced on October 8, 2026 that both the Financial Institutions Near-Term Criteria and FINZ will remain available with no specific end date, abandoning its plan to decide the near-term route's future in 2027. Targets already validated under the Near-Term Criteria stay valid for their full cycle, and SBTi frames the change as aligning with CNZS V2.0, which also permits near-term-only targets. SBTi reports more than 180 financial institutions with validated targets, roughly a third of them banks and about a quarter private equity firms. The announcement also discloses that the FINZ target-setting tool has temporarily stopped calculating technology-share targets for the power sector and emissions-intensity targets for the automotive sector, pending final sector standards.
updates.so_what: Financial-sector filers gain planning certainty, but anyone setting power or automotive portfolio targets should expect to wait for those sector standards before the tool will calculate them.
updates.headline: SBTi drops the end date for its financial-institution target route and pauses two sector calculations
updates.source_title: Financial Institutions Near-Term Criteria to continue without end date

updates.detail: EFRAG announced on October 8, 2026 that Kristian Koktvedgaard becomes Acting Chair of its Sustainability Reporting Board with immediate effect, following Kerstin Lopatta's departure. He serves until the General Assembly appoints a permanent chair on the European Commission's nomination, and no timetable for that appointment is given. EFRAG framed the step as ensuring continuity and singled out timely delivery of technical advice on draft ESRS 40a as the work at stake. The notice gives no reason for the departure.
updates.so_what: A schedule risk rather than a rule change — treat the ESRS 40a advice timetable as slightly less certain than it was.
updates.headline: EFRAG loses its sustainability board chair mid-consultation and names an acting replacement
updates.source_title: EFRAG announces Kristian Koktvedgaard as Acting EFRAG SRB Chair

updates.detail: SBTi released Commitment and Target Statuses V2.1 on October 7, 2026, effective the same day; this is the document that governs how a company holding validated targets is publicly labelled. V2.1 adds a full definition of Expired status, triggered when a target is at least a year past its target year with no new submission, when the mandatory five-year review deadline passes with nothing submitted, when twelve months pass after the review trigger date with no form received, or when a later submission for an expired target fails validation. Expired status attaches to the individual target whose year has passed, not to a company whose later target year is still ahead, and the company rather than SBTi decides whether an expired target needs re-validation. The document also removes the last operative references to the Commitment Compliance Policy, which it formally supersedes, and adds three worked examples in a new annex.
updates.so_what: Check the target year and five-year review date of every validated target you hold — an expired label is public, and avoiding it is a submission deadline rather than a judgment call.
updates.headline: SBTi defines when a validated target expires, and the clock is already running for first-cycle companies
updates.source_title: SBTi Commitment and Target Statuses, Version 2.1 (October 2026)

updates.detail: SBTi released Mandatory Five-Year Review Guidance V2.1 on October 7, 2026, effective the same day, bringing financial institutions into the mandatory review regime. A new annex provides a financial-institution review template mapping each assessment point to the Financial Institutions Near-Term Criteria Version 2.0 and the evidence required for each. The guidance states that for financial institutions in 2026 only, review trigger dates are deferred to December 31, 2026. This is the document whose deadlines feed the expired-target triggers set out in the Commitment and Target Statuses released the same day.
updates.so_what: Financial institutions should treat December 31, 2026 as this year's review trigger date; everyone else should confirm their own trigger date now that missing it carries a public expired label.
updates.headline: SBTi extends its mandatory five-year target review to financial institutions
updates.source_title: SBTi Mandatory Five-Year Review Guidance, Version 2.1 (October 2026)

updates.detail: On October 6, 2026, writing from the UN biodiversity conference COP17, the ISSB announced a webinar on October 22, 2026 to launch an exposure draft proposing a Practice Statement on nature-related disclosures, open for a 120-day consultation closing February 19, 2027. A Practice Statement is a voluntary instrument that helps companies apply IFRS S1 to nature-related risks and opportunities; it is not a new standard and does not amend IFRS S1 or S2, and applying it is not required in order to claim compliance with IFRS Standards. Jurisdictions may nonetheless choose to mandate it, and the proposals draw on the TNFD framework. The exposure draft itself is not yet published: the October 6 announcement fixes the launch date, and no sustainability consultation was open on the IFRS Foundation's website as of October 12, 2026.
updates.so_what: Nature reporting is arriving as a voluntary aid rather than a mandate — read the draft when it lands on October 22 and decide whether to comment before February 19.
updates.headline: The ISSB sets October 22 for the launch of its nature reporting proposals, with comments closing February 19
updates.source_title: Live from COP17: ISSB nature-related disclosures consultation

updates.detail: GHG Protocol published its September Pulse newsletter on October 5, 2026, naming Suzanne Greene as Vice-Chair of its ISB. The newsletter restates that AMI RFI feedback will inform a draft consolidated Corporate Standard slated for public consultation in Quarter 2 2027 — the third primary source giving Q2 rather than the Q3 2027 still shown on the AMI standard web page. On forest carbon it confirms that no forest carbon accounting approach has been selected, responding to press coverage questioning the science and alleging industry influence. It also notes progress toward harmonisation through the ISO partnership and adds two Scope 3 FAQ videos covering data gaps and data types.
updates.so_what: Nothing to act on — but plan for one combined GHG Protocol consultation in Q2 2027 rather than separate Scope 2, Scope 3 and market-instrument rounds.
updates.headline: GHG Protocol's September newsletter names a new standards-board vice-chair and restates the Q2 2027 consultation date

updates.detail: The SEC adopted a final rule on September 30, 2026 amending its quorum requirement, published at 91 FR 62654 and effective on publication, October 2, 2026. A three-member quorum remains the general rule; the amendment provides that where the number of commissioners in office minus those disqualified from a particular matter equals one, that single commissioner constitutes a quorum for that matter. The Commission adopted it without notice and comment, finding that the amendments relate solely to agency management and organisation and are not a substantive rule. The rule says nothing about climate or disclosure, and matters here only because commissioner availability has been a practical constraint on the Commission acting, while the proposed rescission of its climate-disclosure rules remains only proposed.
updates.so_what: No action — but it slightly raises the odds the SEC can finalise the rescission of its climate rule without waiting for a fuller Commission.
updates.headline: The SEC lets a single commissioner act as a quorum when the others are disqualified
updates.source_title: Commission Quorum Requirement, Final Rule, 91 FR 62654 (Oct. 2, 2026)

updates.detail: GHG Protocol's ISB considered the two FCA methods developed by its TWG — Managed Land Proxy Plus and Activity-Based Accounting — and approved neither, stating plainly that no approach has been selected. The open FCA RFI still runs to February 1, 2027, and GHG Protocol says any future method must complete development, testing and public review and secure ISB approval before it can be used. An independent third-party review of the FCA process, commissioned by the Steering Committee Chair after public criticism, found no material breach of its Terms of Reference or due process and no evidence of bias in ISB decision-making; GHG Protocol does not name the reviewer or give a date for the review. Until a method is approved the LSR Standard still does not apply to companies operating on forest land or in forest product value chains.
updates.so_what: If forest land or forest-derived products sit in your value chain, there is still no GHGP method to account for them — plan on your current approach holding through 2027 at least.
updates.headline: GHG Protocol rejects both forest carbon accounting proposals — no method selected
updates.source_title: Forest Carbon Accounting: Where the Process Stands and What Comes Next

updates.detail: SBTi Services published six resources for companies preparing to submit targets under Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0: a preliminary submission form, preliminary data points for the V2.0 target-setting tool, a validation schedule, an updated standard operating procedure, validation procedures and a services glossary. SBTi stated that validation slots for V2.0 submissions open to book from February 1, 2027, replacing the looser 'Q1 2027' it had given before. It also moved the Claims Policy forward into Q4 2026, alongside the new target-setting methods and pathways, the minimum-evidence documentation and the V2.0 explanatory guidance.
updates.so_what: If you are planning a V2.0 submission, work back from February 1, 2027 and use the published procedures to scope the evidence you will need.
updates.headline: SBTi publishes its V2.0 validation pack and names the date target submissions can be booked
updates.source_title: SBTi: Countdown to validation — new resources to prepare for the Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0

updates.detail: The UK's financial regulator finalised Policy Statement PS26/19, applying UK SRS to in-scope listed issuers on a comply-or-explain basis rather than requiring disclosure. The rules apply for accounting periods starting on or after January 1, 2027, so the first reports appear in 2028. Issuers get transitional relief of one year for Scope 3 emissions disclosures and two years for the wider sustainability disclosures under UK SRS S1. The rules replace the regulator's existing climate-reporting requirements for listed issuers and cover the commercial companies, transition, non-equity shares, non-voting equity shares, secondary listing and depositary receipt categories.
updates.so_what: If any group entity is UK-listed, your UK climate reporting basis changes for FY2027 — and comply-or-explain lets you omit an item with a published explanation rather than report it.
updates.headline: The UK adopts ISSB-based reporting for listed companies — comply-or-explain, not a mandate
updates.source_title: PS26/19: Aligning listed issuers' sustainability disclosures with international standards

updates.detail: The EmpCo Directive's rules on environmental claims became applicable across the EU on September 27, 2026, the date written into Directive (EU) 2024/825 itself. From this date, national law implementing the directive bans generic environmental claims such as 'eco-friendly' or 'climate-friendly' where the claimed benefit cannot be demonstrated, and bans claims that a product is carbon neutral, climate neutral or net zero on the basis of offsetting. The obligations cover products already sitting on shelves, not only new launches, although a non-binding common understanding agreed by the national consumer-protection authorities in June 2026 expects good-faith remediation - stickers or point-of-sale corrections - rather than immediate withdrawal of existing stock. Transposition has been uneven, so the national law a claim is judged against still varies by Member State.
updates.so_what: Any consumer-facing carbon-neutral or vague green claim on products sold in the EU is now an enforcement exposure, so sweep live packaging and marketing this quarter rather than at the next redesign.
updates.headline: The EU's ban on vague green claims and offset-based carbon-neutral claims is now live
updates.source_title: Directive (EU) 2024/825 on empowering consumers for the green transition

updates.detail: CEAOB delivered technical advice to the European Commission on an EU-specific limited assurance standard for sustainability reporting, built as carve-outs from and additions to ISSA 5000. It is scoped to limited assurance on the sustainability information required by Article 34(1)(aa) of the Accounting Directive, and the applicable criteria are all the provisions of the ESRS and of the EU Taxonomy Regulation. As advised it would apply to periods beginning on or after December 15, 2027 — a year later than ISSA 5000's own timeline — and it adds a duty to communicate with the statutory auditor plus a 60-day deadline to close engagement files after the report is issued. The advice feeds a future Commission delegated act under Article 26a of the Audit Directive, and no adoption date is given.
updates.so_what: Expect EU sustainability assurance to run on an EU-modified ISSA 5000 — ask your assurance provider which carve-outs change the evidence they will request.
updates.headline: EU advisers propose a Europe-specific limited assurance standard for sustainability reports
updates.source_title: CEAOB Technical Advice: Standard for Limited Assurance on Sustainability Reporting

updates.detail: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/1560, which establishes the Voluntary Sustainability Reporting Standard (VSRS), entered into force on September 24, 2026 — the third day after its Official Journal publication, per its Article 4. The VSRS is the standard that anchors the CSRD value-chain cap: an in-scope reporter cannot demand more sustainability information from a smaller value-chain partner than this standard contains. Its value-chain-cap article applies to financial years beginning on or after January 1, 2027, but the standard itself is available for any company outside mandatory scope to use now. Note the split: the voluntary standard is in force from September 24, 2026, while the mandatory revised ESRS enter into force on November 10, 2026.
updates.so_what: Use the VSRS as the ceiling for what you ask suppliers below the CSRD threshold to provide — it is now the published limit, not a draft.
updates.headline: The EU's new voluntary reporting standard is already in force, ahead of the mandatory one
updates.source_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/1560 — voluntary sustainability reporting standard

updates.detail: Version 2.0 of the SBTi Commitment and Target Statuses document carried an effective date of September 24, 2026, and on that date it superseded the Commitment Compliance Policy as the governing rulebook for how companies appear on the public Target Dashboard. The dashboard now presents three headline status groups — validated targets, commitment to set targets, and commitment removed — with revised status terminology, updated reasons, and region classifications aligned to the UN M49 geographic scheme in both the interactive view and the downloadable datasets. SBTi published no go-live announcement or changelog on or after September 24, so confirmation rests on the document's own effective date plus the dashboard now matching the new scheme. A 'target expired' status is defined in the statuses document but is not visible as a label on the public dashboard page.
updates.so_what: Check how your company and your key suppliers and customers now display on the dashboard, because the status label is what stakeholders and data vendors will scrape from this week on.
updates.headline: SBTi's new company status system took effect, retiring the Commitment Compliance Policy
updates.source_title: SBTi Commitment and Target Statuses, Version 2.0 (August 2026)

updates.detail: At its September 24, 2026 meeting the ISSB reached the scheduled decision point on its Human Capital research project and decided, with all 12 members in agreement, to rename it 'Workforce-related Disclosures' to better reflect its scope. Staff also set out five areas of continued research — terminology, investor information needs, the link between business models and workforce risk, jurisdictional factors, and emerging practice under IFRS S1 — but the ISSB was not asked to decide whether to open standard-setting, and deciding the project's direction remains its next milestone. A separate paper summarised the July 2026 Transition Implementation Group discussion of the undefined term 'targets' in IFRS S2: staff analysis concluded that climate-related targets extend beyond GHG emissions to other climate risks and opportunities, and that an item need not be labelled a target or board-approved to qualify. Transition Implementation Group discussion is not authoritative guidance.
updates.so_what: Re-read what you disclose as climate targets under IFRS S2 — energy, water or resilience goals may belong there, not just emissions targets. No workforce standard is in prospect yet.
updates.headline: ISSB renames its workforce project; a staff paper revisits what counts as a climate 'target'
updates.source_title: ISSB meeting, 24 September 2026 — agenda and papers

updates.detail: GHG Protocol released the complete summary of responses to its Actions and Market Instruments Request for Information on September 23, 2026, closing the gap left by July's preliminary readout. It reports 437 valid responses gathered between March 31 and June 15, 2026: 84% strongly support or support the proposed multi-statement structure, 86% agree with its stated purpose, 87% want a market-based GHG inventory statement included, and 80% want a GHG impact statement. The clear outlier is the proposed non-GHG indicators statement, backed by only 33% with 25% opposed. Respondents pressed for clear quality criteria and for the new statements to stay optional at first while data readiness catches up; GHG Protocol restates a draft consolidated Corporate Standard for consultation in Q2 2027 and a final in Q4 2028, both still its own estimates.
updates.so_what: Plan on reporting contractual and market-instrument emissions separately from your physical inventory — the direction now has documented majority support, so the question is the detail, not the shape.
updates.headline: GHG Protocol publishes the full AMI feedback summary: strong support for splitting the inventory into separate statements
updates.source_title: GHG Protocol Releases AMI Feedback Summary Showing Broad Support for Proposed Multi-Statement Reporting Framework

updates.detail: Trade press reported on September 23–24, 2026 that ISO/DIS 14060, the first international standard defining what a net-zero aligned organization is, did not clear its Draft International Standard (DIS) ballot. The 12-week ballot closed on September 10, 2026 with 88 countries participating and roughly 5,000 comments submitted; ISO confirmed only that the draft 'did not receive the level of approval required to advance in its current form' and does not publish tallies or national votes. Passage requires two-thirds approval of participating members with no more than a quarter of votes cast against. The draft returns to ISO/TC 207/SC 7, which will decide how to revise and recirculate it, with finalisation now anticipated in 2027 and no date disclosed. Reporting that fossil-fuel-producing countries drove the opposition rests on anonymous sources and is unconfirmed.
updates.so_what: Do not anchor net-zero claim language to an ISO definition yet — treat SBTi's V2.0 criteria as the operative benchmark for at least another year.
updates.headline: ISO's draft net-zero standard fails its first international ballot and goes back to committee
updates.source_title: ISO members send net-zero draft back for revisions (Trellis, 23 September 2026)

updates.detail: CARB resubmitted the SB 253/261 initial regulation to the Office of Administrative Law on September 21, 2026, three months after withdrawing it in June for modifications. It appears on OAL's review list as file 2026-0921-06, logged as a regular resubmittal. OAL has up to 30 working days to review it, which runs to roughly November 2, 2026 — about a week before the November 10 reporting deadline the regulation itself sets. CARB has asked OAL to let the regulation take effect the moment it is filed with the Secretary of State, because the default effective date would otherwise fall after November 10. This is the last procedural gate on the November 10 deadline.
updates.so_what: Keep building to Nov 10. The approval, not the filing, is what locks the date, so watch for it through early November.
updates.headline: California's climate-disclosure regulation reaches the state's final legal reviewer
updates.source_title: California Office of Administrative Law: Proposed Regulations Under Review (ARB file 2026-0921-06, filed Sept 21, 2026)

updates.detail: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/1563, which amends the 2023 ESRS to cut mandatory datapoints by more than 60%, was published in the Official Journal on September 21, 2026. Its Article 3 sets a fixed entry into force of November 10, 2026 and application to financial years beginning on or after January 1, 2027 — so the November date is now statutory text, not an expectation drawn from an unpublished draft. Article 2 gives companies already in scope a three-way election for financial years beginning in 2026: apply the revised standards in full, or apply the 2023 standards with specified reliefs covering materiality-assessment flexibility, undue cost or effort, and acquisition and disposal timing — and state in the sustainability statement which version was used. The two-month scrutiny period expired with no objection tabled in the Parliament or Council.
updates.so_what: Decide now which version you apply for FY2026 and get the disclosure of that choice into your reporting plan — the election is explicit in the regulation and you have to state it.
updates.headline: The slimmed-down EU reporting standards are law: published in the Official Journal, in force November 10, 2026
updates.source_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/1563 of 3 July 2026 amending Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2772 as regards the simplification of certain sustainability reporting standards

updates.detail: EFRAG released a draft XBRL taxonomy for the revised ESRS on September 17, 2026 and opened it for public comment until November 11, 2026. The taxonomy defines how each disclosure in the revised standards would be tagged so a sustainability statement can be read by software rather than only by people, and it replaces an earlier draft issued in August 2024. EFRAG states plainly that digital tagging of ESRS disclosures is not yet mandatory, because ESMA and the European Commission have still to establish the framework that would require it. EFRAG intends to submit the final taxonomy to ESMA and the Commission by the end of 2026.
updates.so_what: Nothing to file yet, but this draft is the clearest preview of the structure your disclosure tooling will eventually have to produce, so route it to whoever owns reporting systems.
updates.headline: EFRAG opens consultation on the machine-readable tagging rules for the revised EU standards
updates.source_title: EFRAG Releases Draft ESRS XBRL Taxonomy for the Revised ESRS and Launches Public Consultation

updates.detail: EFRAG held its United States outreach session on the draft ESRS 40a standard on September 17, 2026, and the event page now shows a recording link in place of a registration form. EFRAG has published no written summary of the session, so the recording is the only account of it available. Further jurisdiction sessions run through the autumn, including Brazil on September 21, New Zealand on September 22, Japan and Canada on September 25, the United Kingdom on September 29, and a worldwide session on October 12. The cost-benefit survey was extended to October 18, 2026 and the exposure draft consultation itself closed October 31, 2026.
updates.so_what: If your group would report under Article 40a, watch the US recording before drafting comments and treat October 11 and October 31 as the dates to work back from.
updates.headline: The US session on the non-EU parent standard has been held, and the two deadlines that matter are now weeks away
updates.source_title: Save the Dates: EFRAG Outreach Events on the ESRS for Certain Non-EU Undertakings

updates.detail: On September 15, 2026 the European Parliament adopted its first-reading position on extending CBAM from raw materials to the downstream goods made from them, such as finished steel and aluminium products. Parliament would cover 457 downstream product categories, against the 180 the European Commission proposed in December 2025 and around 200 in the Council general approach of June 2026. The file has been referred back to committee for negotiations with the Council, so the final product list is unsettled and will land somewhere in that range. Parliament also attached anti-circumvention measures to the scope extension.
updates.so_what: If you import metal parts or finished goods into the EU, assume CBAM exposure may reach well beyond today's raw-material list and start mapping which customs codes could be caught.
updates.headline: European Parliament votes to more than double the goods the EU carbon border tax would cover
updates.source_title: Legislative Observatory procedure file 2025/0419(COD): CBAM, extension of scope to downstream goods

updates.detail: ISO 14068:2026, 'Climate change management — Carbon neutrality', was published on September 11, 2026 according to its ISO stage record, and ISO 14068-1:2023 is now listed as withdrawn. It is the standard a company is pointed to when it wants to make a carbon neutrality claim about an organization, product or activity using offsetting, and it sits alongside rather than inside the GHG Protocol consolidation track. The publication landed sixteen days before the EU's EmpCo rules banned offset-based carbon-neutral claims on consumer products, so the standard and the EU consumer-law position now point in different directions for consumer-facing claims. Note that both of ISO's own pages for this standard still lag: the public page shows it under publication and the committee view shows an earlier drafting stage. The publication itself, and the withdrawal of the 2023 edition, appear in ISO's project records.
updates.so_what: If you make or verify carbon neutrality claims outside consumer marketing, move your methodology reference to ISO 14068:2026 — and check separately that consumer-facing claims survive the EU ban.
updates.headline: ISO publishes a consolidated carbon neutrality standard, withdrawing the 2023 version

updates.detail: EFRAG launched an online questionnaire on September 11, 2026 collecting expected costs and benefits of the draft ESRS 40a standard, which would govern reporting by non-EU parent undertakings caught by Article 40a of the EU Accounting Directive. Responses closed October 18, 2026 at 23:59 CEST, after EFRAG extended the deadline from October 11 — two weeks before the exposure draft's own consultation deadline of October 31. External consultants will turn the responses into a cost-benefit analysis that EFRAG publishes alongside its final technical advice to the European Commission. EFRAG is explicitly asking non-EU companies in scope to respond, and offers a downloadable PDF of the questionnaire alongside the online form.
updates.so_what: If your US parent would report under Article 40a, put cost estimates on paper by October 11 — this survey, not the October 31 consultation, is where the burden case gets quantified.
updates.headline: EFRAG opens a cost-benefit survey aimed at the non-EU parents that would report under Article 40a
updates.source_title: EFRAG: Call for public input on cost-benefit analysis for the exposure draft ESRS for certain non-EU undertakings

updates.detail: The SBTi's second public consultation on the updated draft Power Sector Net-Zero Standard closed on September 7, 2026, after a deadline extension announced August 14. SBTi says it will now run a pilot with participating companies using real-world data, and that consultation and pilot findings together will inform refinement before Technical Council approval and Board of Trustees adoption — no date is published for either step. Electric utilities are told to keep using the Quick Start Guide for Electric Utilities in the meantime. With the separate call for evidence on high-emitting sectors also closed on September 11, the Forest, Land and Agriculture call for evidence — open until October 8, 2026 — is now the only SBTi input window still listed as open.
updates.so_what: Power-sector filers should expect V2-aligned criteria to land with little notice; anyone with land or agriculture in their footprint has until October 8 to submit evidence.
updates.headline: Power sector consultation closes; a pilot comes next, with no published date for the final standard
updates.source_title: SBTi: Second public consultation on updated draft Power Sector Net-Zero Standard

updates.detail: The revised ESRS delegated act, adopted July 3, 2026, was sent to the European Parliament and Council for a scrutiny period of two months that can be extended once by a further two months. That initial window lapsed on September 3 with no objection, no recorded extension decision and no Official Journal entry; the Commission's delegated-acts register still listed the act as not in force as of September 7. The adopted text's own entry-into-force clause is drafted as the adoption date plus four months and one week — November 10, 2026 — indicating the Commission planned for the full extended window.
updates.so_what: Keep planning for mandatory application to financial years starting in 2027 with optional early application for 2026; nothing binds until the Official Journal entry appears.
updates.headline: Revised EU standards pass the two-month scrutiny mark unpublished, leaving November entry into force intact
updates.source_title: European Commission: CSRD implementing and delegated acts register

updates.detail: CARB released a guidance document for 2026 SB 253 reporting submittals and opened a voluntary online intake platform, with email submission still accepted. Companies may file an existing annual report containing Scope 1 and Scope 2 figures, data already reported to another program, CARB's draft template, or — for entities that were not collecting data as of December 5, 2024 — a statement of non-reporting on company letterhead. No particular emission-factor dataset is mandated for this cycle, and CARB confirmed that under first-year enforcement discretion it will accept submissions that have not been third-party assured. The guidance rests on a regulation that is still not approved: the Office of Administrative Law's rolling list of filings under review showed no climate-disclosure submission from CARB as of September 7, 2026.
updates.so_what: Start assembling the November 10 filing now — the format bar is deliberately low, so internal review time, not data quality, is the binding constraint.
updates.headline: CARB publishes first-cycle reporting guidance and opens a voluntary submission platform
updates.source_title: CARB: Guidance Document for SB 253 2026 Reporting Submittals

updates.detail: EFRAG announced seven jurisdiction-specific outreach events on the ESRS 40a exposure draft — the standard that would govern reporting by non-EU parent undertakings caught by Article 40a of the EU Accounting Directive. The US session is set for September 17, 2026, with further sessions covering Mexico, Korea, New Zealand, Japan, Canada and the UK. The underlying public consultation opened July 23, 2026 and closes October 31, 2026, with EFRAG's technical advice to the Commission due January 2027.
updates.so_what: If your US parent would report under Article 40a rather than through an EU subsidiary, join the September 17 session and file comments before October 31.
updates.headline: EFRAG schedules jurisdiction outreach on the standard for non-EU parents, with a US session on September 17
updates.source_title: EFRAG: Save the dates — outreach events on the ESRS for certain non-EU undertakings

updates.detail: The Modified Regulations CARB adopted on July 27, 2026 reset the first Scope 1 and Scope 2 reporting deadline to November 10, 2026, but they become legally effective only once the Office of Administrative Law (OAL) approves the package and files it with the Secretary of State. OAL's daily-updated review list, checked on August 31, 2026, shows three Air Resources Board submissions pending: the cap-and-trade programme, the separate facility-level Mandatory Reporting Regulation (filed July 31, before the corporate-programme comment period even closed on August 11), and Advanced Clean Fleets and Low Carbon Fuel Standard amendments. None of them is the corporate climate-disclosure regulation. OAL has up to 30 working days to review a package once submitted, so November 10 remains reachable, but the margin is narrowing.
updates.so_what: Keep building your Scope 1 and 2 submission to the November 10 date, but hold it as contingent rather than fixed: it is not legally locked until OAL approves, and nothing had been filed as of today.
updates.headline: California's reset reporting deadline still awaits its final legal step, with 10 weeks to go
updates.source_title: California Office of Administrative Law, Proposed Regulations Under Review (checked Aug 31, 2026)

updates.detail: The EFRAG secretariat published the 2026 Draft List of ESRS Datapoints, a workbook of every datapoint definition under the revised European Sustainability Reporting Standards the Commission adopted on July 3, 2026, together with an explanatory note. A draft XBRL taxonomy for digital tagging will be published separately later, with its own public consultation. It succeeds the earlier IG 3 datapoint list and reflects the roughly 60 percent cut in mandatory datapoints. The review is scoped to methodology and fatal flaws rather than general redrafting, runs through an online survey, and closes on October 23, 2026. A final version is expected by the end of 2026.
updates.so_what: This is the list your reporting system will actually be built against. Have whoever owns ESRS tagging check it against your data model before the October 23 review closes.
updates.headline: EFRAG opens a fatal-flaw review of the full datapoint list for the revised EU standards
updates.source_title: EFRAG Secretariat Releases 2026 Draft List of Datapoints for Revised ESRS

updates.detail: The complete Summary of Feedback (version 1.1) for the Scope 2 consultation was posted to the Standards Development and Governance Repository, superseding the executive summary released on July 29, 2026. It synthesises roughly 1,100 responses from 56 countries, about 62 percent of them from companies, industry groups and consultants, gathered between October 20, 2025 and January 31, 2026. The dominant themes are the trade-off between integrity and feasibility, implementation burden on smaller reporters, regional gaps in the hourly and location-specific data the proposals would require, assurance complexity, and the risk of misalignment with EU, UK and Australian reporting rules. GHG Protocol says the feedback will directly inform the next phase of technical working group development and Independent Standards Board review. No decision on hourly matching or the emission-factor hierarchy has been made.
updates.so_what: No action, but the case for scenario-planning both hourly matching and the status quo now rests on GHG Protocol's own document rather than on press reports.
updates.headline: GHG Protocol publishes the full Scope 2 consultation feedback summary
updates.source_title: GHG Protocol, Scope 2 Public Consultation Summary of Feedback (v1.1, Aug 25, 2026)

updates.detail: The Commission released guidance for CBAM verifiers and the national accreditation bodies that accredit them, plus a procedure for verifier access to the CBAM Registry. It elaborates the existing accreditation and verification rules rather than creating new obligations. The published sequence runs: national bodies began CBAM accreditation in April 2026; accredited verifiers can register in the CBAM Registry and start first verifications, including documentation review and site visits, from September 2026; they can issue first verification reports from January 2027; declarants can buy certificates from February 2027 and finalise the 2026 declaration in September 2027. The first verifier was accredited on September 23, 2026 by Greece's national accreditation body; the Commission's official list had not yet been published.
updates.so_what: If you import covered goods into the EU, confirm now that your verifier is in the accreditation pipeline. No verification report can be issued before January 2027, and your 2026 declaration depends on one.
updates.headline: Commission publishes CBAM verification and accreditation guidance; verifier registry access opens in September
updates.source_title: European Commission, Guidance on CBAM verification and accreditation (Aug 24, 2026)

updates.detail: The Trustees approved operating and financing plans covering 2027-2031 that put ISSB on a longer-term, shared funding base. They also approved opening an ISSB office in Geneva, expected mid-2027 and proposed that each board comprise 10 members from 2028. Proposed amendments to the Foundation's Constitution are open for public comment until November 16, 2026. No reporting standard or effective date changed.
updates.so_what: Nothing to implement, but if you want a say in how ISSB is governed and resourced, the Constitution consultation closes November 16, 2026.
updates.headline: IFRS Foundation Trustees approve a five-year plan and open a consultation on Constitution changes
updates.source_title: IFRS Foundation Trustees announce five-year plan

updates.detail: SBTi published a consolidated call for participation covering four open processes that will shape its next generation of sector standards. The four windows are a Call for Evidence on high-emitting sectors including aluminium, aviation and steel (closes September 11, 2026); the second public consultation on the draft Power Sector Net-Zero Standard (closes September 7, 2026); an expression of interest for FLAG regional stakeholder convenings (closed September 11, 2026, extended from September 8); and a Call for Evidence informing FLAG Standard V2 (closes October 8, 2026). The Power consultation deadline was extended from August 31 to September 7 to allow more considered feedback. None of this creates a requirement today — these are the formal windows for influencing criteria that will bind sector-exposed companies from 2027 onward.
updates.so_what: If your emissions sit in power, agriculture, forestry or a heavy-emitting sector, assign an owner this week — the windows close between September 7 and October 8 and are the cheapest chance to shape criteria you will later have to meet.
updates.headline: SBTi opens four concurrent input windows on Power, FLAG and high-emitting sector standards
updates.source_title: SBTi: Get involved today — your chance to help shape the next generation of SBTi Standards

updates.detail: The European Commission released four general guides covering CBAM concepts, a quick guide for non-EU operators, methods for calculating emissions embedded in goods, and the free-allocation adjustment to the number of certificates surrendered. Six sector-specific guides accompany them, for cement, hydrogen, fertilisers, iron and steel, aluminium and electricity. The documents are non-binding but set out, with worked examples, how the Commission expects the definitive-regime rules to be applied. Much of the material is aimed at non-EU operators who must supply embedded-emissions data to EU importers.
updates.so_what: Send the relevant sector guide to whoever produces your embedded-emissions data for EU-bound goods, well before the first certificate surrender in 2027.
updates.headline: Commission publishes ten CBAM guidance documents for the definitive regime
updates.source_title: European Commission publishes a series of guidance documents to support CBAM implementation in the definitive period

updates.detail: The SEC's semiannual Regulatory Flexibility Agenda, published in the Federal Register, carries the rescission of the 2024 climate-related disclosure rules (RIN 3235-AN76) at the proposed rule stage. It records the June 3, 2026 proposal and the August 3, 2026 comment close, but states no target date for final action. The absence of a timetable means the rescission had no committed adoption date as of mid-August 2026.
updates.so_what: Do not plan around a specific rescission date; the SEC's August 31 status report to the Eighth Circuit is the next real signal on timing.
updates.headline: SEC regulatory agenda lists the climate-rule rescission with no date for final action
updates.source_title: Regulatory Flexibility Agenda (Securities and Exchange Commission)

updates.detail: Media reporting (Fortune) on the ~1,100-response Scope 2 consultation: only about 22% of all respondents — and 12% of the 429 responding companies — supported the proposed hourly matching requirement, with the Clean Energy Buyers Association — since renamed the Corporate Energy Buyers Association — publicly opposed. The electricity accounting working group is reportedly scheduled to meet in September 2026 to address the pushback. Not an official GHGP publication and no decision has been made — but it reinforces why this workstream carries medium confidence: the market-based accounting outcome is genuinely open.
updates.so_what: No action — but scenario-plan for both hourly matching and status-quo market-based accounting; don't rebuild procurement strategy on a rule that may not land.
updates.headline: Reported consultation tallies show broad opposition to Scope 2 hourly matching

updates.detail: A companion blog post to the Five-Year Review explainer details the September 24, 2026 Target Dashboard changes: revised company status terminology, updated commitment- and target-level status classifications, and regional classifications aligned to the UN M49 standard. Once effective, the revised Commitment and Target Statuses Document supersedes the existing Commitment Compliance Policy — status labels visible to investors and civil society will change for companies on the public dashboard.
updates.so_what: Check how your company's public dashboard status will read after Sept 24 — investors and NGOs will see the new labels.
updates.headline: SBTi Target Dashboard status overhaul: Commitment Compliance Policy superseded Sept 24

updates.detail: New explainer on the revised Mandatory Five-Year Review Guidance and Commitment & Target Statuses Document: 6-month review form / 12-month revised-target deadlines, case-by-case extensions for companies moving to V2.0, and status assessment only at the 12-month deadline. ~300 of 11,600+ companies with validated targets must complete reviews by end of 2026. Dashboard changes (new status terminology, UN M49 regions) go live September 24, 2026.
updates.so_what: If your targets hit their 5-year mark, calendar the 6-month review form and 12-month revised-target deadlines — ~300 companies must complete reviews by end of 2026.
updates.headline: SBTi details updated Five-Year Review Guidance; Target Dashboard overhaul set for Sept 24

updates.detail: Signals continued convergence between ESRS GHG accounting guidance and the PCAF financed-emissions methodology (which GHGP's draft Scope 3 revision also aligns to for Category 15). No new requirement or deadline — a monitor-only item for non-financial reporters.
updates.so_what: Monitor-only unless you report financed emissions.
updates.headline: EFRAG joins the PCAF Engagement Group for central banks and financial regulators

updates.detail: Monthly newsletter summarizing the July 29 GHGP–ISO consolidation, Scope 2 consultation results, AMI multi-statement support, LSR Guidance availability, the Forest Carbon Accounting RFI (open through Feb 1, 2027), and the Amsterdam AMI TWG meeting. No new milestones announced.
updates.so_what: Recap only — nothing new to action.
updates.headline: GHG Protocol Pulse (August) recaps consolidation announcement

updates.detail: Steven Maijoor becomes IFRS Foundation Trustees Chair from January 1, 2027 and Sam Woods becomes IASB Chair from October 1, 2026. Emmanuel Faber continues as ISSB Chair, so no change to sustainability standard-setting direction — governance continuity for the body that will decide whether IFRS S2 migrates to the revised GHG Protocol standards.
updates.so_what: No action — leadership continuity at the ISSB.
updates.headline: IFRS Foundation names new Trustees and IASB chairs; Faber stays at ISSB

updates.detail: The 15-day comment window on the July 27 Modified Regulations (which reset the first Scope 1/2 deadline to November 10, 2026) closed as scheduled. As of August 31, the package had not yet appeared on the Office of Administrative Law's under-review list — resubmission and OAL approval, which make the November 10 deadline legally effective, remain pending. CARB's guidance and voluntary intake platform are still targeted for ~September 1; the next sector listening session is August 26.
updates.so_what: Hold Nov 10 as your working deadline, but watch for OAL approval — and don't stand down Scope 1/2 data collection.
updates.headline: Comment period closes on CARB's Modified Regulations

updates.detail: Recruitment window closed for new ISB seats targeting civil society, academia, and research, with geographic focus on North America, Latin America, and Africa.
updates.so_what: No corporate action.
updates.headline: GHGP Independent Standards Board application deadline passes

updates.detail: The revised standard ISO 14068, Climate change management - Carbon neutrality, advanced to stage 60.00, international standard under publication, on August 7, 2026. It will replace ISO 14068-1:2023, and ISO lists expected publication in September 2026. The standard sets the principles and requirements an organization or product is measured against when it claims carbon neutrality, including how reductions and offsets are quantified and disclosed.
updates.so_what: Have legal and marketing review existing carbon-neutral claim language against the new edition once it publishes - it lands days before the EU's EmpCo claim bans apply on September 27, 2026.
updates.headline: ISO 14068 on carbon neutrality moves to publication, expected September 2026
updates.source_title: ISO/FDIS 14068 - Climate change management - Carbon neutrality

updates.detail: First of six sector-specific sessions (Aug 5 – Sep 9, 2026) gathering industry input on Scope 3 categories and assurance for the Subsequent Rulemaking covering 2027+ reporting.
updates.so_what: If California Scope 3 hits you in 2027, get your sector's concerns on record now (sessions run through Sep 9).
updates.headline: CARB begins sector listening sessions for the 2027 rulemaking

updates.detail: The 60-day comment window on the proposed full rescission of the 2024 climate disclosure rules ended. The SEC owes the Eighth Circuit a status report by August 31, 2026; final rescission action is queued, likely late 2026.
updates.so_what: No federal obligations coming — keep climate-risk materiality assessments current under the pre-2024 framework.
updates.headline: Comment period closes on SEC rescission proposal

updates.detail: Revision of the Forest, Land and Agriculture Standard begins: stakeholder-meeting expressions of interest due September 8, evidence submissions due October 8, 2026. FLAG V2 will integrate CNZS V2.0 innovations and align with the GHG Protocol Land Sector & Removals Standard — a direct cross-framework dependency.
updates.so_what: Land-exposed companies: submit evidence by Oct 8 and start reconciling FLAG targets with GHGP land-sector accounting.
updates.headline: SBTi opens call for input on FLAG Standard V2

updates.detail: The headline governance decision of the revision cycle: Corporate Standard, Scope 2 Guidance, Scope 3 Standard, AMI, and ISO 14064-1 merge into one standard (Part 1: physical inventory; Part 2: actions & market instruments). Integrated public consultation planned Q2 2027; final publication estimated Q4 2028. Published alongside an updated Standard Development Plan, FAQ, Scope 2 consultation feedback summary (~1,100 responses from 56 countries), and preliminary AMI RFI findings (~500 responses).
updates.so_what: Plan for one global corporate standard by ~2029 — budget a gap assessment before the Q2 2027 consultation.
updates.headline: GHGP and ISO confirm single co-branded corporate standard

updates.detail: Digital tagging taxonomy update reflecting the GHG emissions disclosure amendments; comments due September 28, 2026 — keeping digital reporting aligned ahead of the January 1, 2027 effective date.
updates.so_what: Digital-tagging teams: comment by Sep 28; expect updated tags in time for FY2027 reporting.
updates.headline: ISSB proposes Taxonomy Update for the December 2025 S2 amendments

updates.detail: Modified Regulations released with a 15-day comment period: the first Scope 1/2 report deadline moves from August 10 to November 10, 2026 (proposed as the fixed annual date going forward); fee-determination notices move to December 10, 2026; insurer inclusion proposed for 2027.
updates.so_what: Three extra months for first Scope 1/2 reports — spend them on assurance-readiness, not delay.
updates.headline: CARB resets first SB 253 deadline to November 10, 2026

updates.detail: Single-materiality standard for non-EU parents with >€450m EU turnover; reporting from FY2028 (first reports 2029). Consultation closed October 31, 2026 — directly relevant to US-headquartered multinationals.
updates.so_what: Non-EU parents with >€450m EU turnover: your FY2028 EU reporting template is on the table — comment by Oct 31.
updates.headline: EFRAG publishes ESRS 40a exposure draft for non-EU groups

updates.detail: All 12 board members approved due-process steps for the nature-related disclosures Practice Statement exposure draft (120-day comment period, publication planned October 2026); the board also voted 12-0 to enhance six SASB Standards in Technology & Communications.
updates.so_what: Nature disclosure stays voluntary practice guidance, not a new mandatory standard; tech companies should watch the SASB metric changes.
updates.headline: ISSB clears nature exposure draft for October; adds six tech-sector SASB standards

updates.detail: Workshop proposals: Scope 3 limited to five mandatory categories (1, 3, 5, 6, 7) from 2027; limited assurance for Scope 1/2 from 2027 escalating to reasonable by 2030; mandatory template abandoned for a voluntary intake platform. CARB stated SB 253 reporting 'will not dynamically update to reflect GHG Protocol developments' — pinning California to current GHGP versions even as they are revised.
updates.so_what: Build California reporting on today's GHGP versions — and expect to run dual methodologies once revised GHGP publishes.
updates.headline: CARB previews 2027+ framework and locks GHG Protocol versions

updates.detail: Updated draft aligned with CNZS V2.0: emissions-intensity-based low-carbon power definitions, IEA WEO 2024 NZE pathways, scope 1 (generators) and scope 3 (retailers) approaches. Open through September 7, 2026 (extended August 14 from August 31); pilot testing follows.
updates.so_what: Power-sector companies: respond by Sept 7 — target-setting metrics are changing.
updates.headline: Second consultation opens on Power Sector Net-Zero Standard

updates.detail: Service covering Category A/B determination, target mapping to V2.0, and inventory/assurance gap analysis — explicitly not pre-validation.
updates.so_what: Optional gap-check; the free Main Changes Document covers most of the same ground.
updates.headline: SBTi Services launches V2.0 Readiness Assessment

updates.detail: Mandatory datapoints cut by more than 60% (total by 70%+), ~30% estimated cost reduction per company. Mandatory for FY2027, optional early adoption FY2026. A companion delegated act establishes the voluntary (VSME-based) standard anchoring the value-chain cap. Now in the Parliament/Council scrutiny period; entry into force expected ~November 2026.
updates.so_what: Re-scope your CSRD program against the slimmed datapoints; weigh FY2026 early adoption.
updates.headline: Commission adopts revised ESRS delegated act

updates.detail: 20-chapter implementation guidance with worked examples and 10 corporate case studies; v1.1 contains minor non-substantive edits. Forest carbon accounting deferred pending an RFI open until February 1, 2027, covering activity-based accounting, managed land proxies, and non-zero reference levels.
updates.so_what: Screen for land/biogenic/removals exposure before the Jan 1, 2027 effective date; forestry-exposed companies should answer the RFI by Feb 1, 2027.
updates.headline: LSR Guidance and Standard v1.1 published; Forest Carbon RFI opens

updates.detail: The initial regulation package (submitted May 20) was pulled back for clarifying changes six weeks before the then-applicable August 10 deadline, with a simultaneous announcement that the deadline would move to November 10; the July 27 Modified Regulations put the new date into regulatory text.
updates.so_what: Superseded — the July 27 package reset the deadline to Nov 10.
updates.headline: CARB withdraws regulation from OAL for modifications

updates.detail: Preliminary feedback shows strong support for the multi-statement reporting model separating physical inventory, market-based inventory, and GHG impact statements. Full feedback summary due 'in coming months.'
updates.so_what: Expect market-instrument reporting to become separate statements — stop designing systems that net certificates against inventory.
updates.headline: AMI White Paper RFI closes after an extension to June 15, with ~500 responses

updates.detail: General approach endorses extending CBAM to downstream iron/steel/aluminium goods with a refined product list, pre-consumer scrap anti-circumvention, a crisis-exemption mechanism, and mandatory annual scope reviews. EP's ENVI committee backed expansion July 6 (report tabled July 9); trilogue agreement targeted by end-2026.
updates.so_what: Importers of finished steel/aluminium goods: model 2028 cost exposure now — scope is expanding.
updates.headline: Council agrees position on CBAM downstream expansion

updates.detail: The final standard lands after two consultations and two pilot phases: Category A/B classification, separate scope target structures, significance-based scope 3 boundary (≥5% categories), formalized limited assurance for Category A, and the Ongoing Emissions Responsibility framework. Validation opens Feb 1, 2027; V1.3.1 available until January 31, 2028; V2.0-only from February 1, 2028.
updates.so_what: Map your targets to Category A/B requirements and decide V1.3.1 vs V2.0 submission before validation opens Feb 1, 2027.
updates.headline: SBTi publishes Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0

updates.detail: Release Nos. 33-11421 / 34-105572: complete rescission of the stayed 2024 rules on grounds of statutory overreach and unjustified costs, returning to the pre-2024 principles-based materiality framework. No replacement rule proposed.
updates.so_what: Plan on no federal climate rule; California, the EU, and ISSB jurisdictions now drive US disclosure obligations.
updates.headline: SEC proposes full rescission of 2024 climate disclosure rules

updates.detail: Draft delegated act and VSME-based voluntary standard published for public comment following EFRAG's technical advice, setting up formal adoption in July.
updates.so_what: Superseded by the July 3 adoption.
updates.headline: Commission releases draft revised-ESRS delegated act for feedback

updates.detail: Nature-related requirements will be proposed as an IFRS Practice Statement building on TNFD rather than a new mandatory standard — complementing S1/S2 without amending them. Exposure draft planned October 2026.
updates.so_what: No new mandatory nature standard — TNFD-aligned guidance instead; existing TNFD work carries over.
updates.headline: ISSB chooses Practice Statement route for nature disclosures

updates.detail: The JWG will develop a harmonized product carbon footprint standard building on ISO 14067 and the GHGP Product Life Cycle Standard, drawing on 450+ expert submissions from 410+ organizations in 50+ countries.
updates.so_what: Product carbon footprint methods will converge — avoid over-customizing PCF tooling to any single standard.
updates.headline: ISO–GHGP Joint Working Group finalized for product-level standard

updates.detail: Headline proposals with 80-100% TWG support: disaggregation by data type, verification-status disclosure, 95% minimum inclusion with annual 100% quantification, Category 15 narrowed to financed emissions, and a proposed new Category 16 for facilitated activities. All explicitly draft.
updates.so_what: Start tagging Scope 3 data by type, method, and verification status — auditable metadata is where this is heading.
updates.headline: Scope 3 Phase 1 Progress Update published (provisional)

updates.detail: White paper proposes the multi-statement reporting model: physical inventory, market-based inventory (commodity certificates), consequential GHG impact statement, and optional non-GHG indicators — with no netting between statements.
updates.so_what: Inventory and instrument claims will separate; keep certificate data (vintage, geography, contract) clean and distinct.
updates.headline: AMI Phase 1 White Paper published; 60-day RFI opens

updates.detail: Second exposure draft covering agriculture and power-sector standards plus the IFRS S2 Industry-based Guidance.
updates.so_what: Monitor if you use SASB agriculture or power-sector metrics.
updates.headline: ISSB proposes amendments to three more SASB Standards

updates.detail: Directive (EU) 2026/470 takes effect: CSRD scope narrowed to >1,000 employees AND >€450m turnover, value-chain cap live, limited assurance permanent. Member State transposition due March 19, 2027.
updates.so_what: Re-check whether you're still in CSRD scope (>1,000 employees AND >€450m); value-chain data requests are now capped.
updates.headline: Omnibus I directive enters into force

updates.detail: First-in-nation mandatory corporate GHG reporting regulation approved, with Scope 1/2 reports then due August 10, 2026 (later reset to November 10). Insurers exempt for 2026; SB 261 provisions included despite the injunction.
updates.so_what: This locked the regime's shape: >$1B revenue, GHGP-based, fee program, assurance phase-in.
updates.headline: CARB Board approves initial SB 253/261 regulation

updates.detail: Final legislative step after Parliament's December 16 vote and Council's February 24 adoption — the Omnibus saga formally concludes.
