updates.so_what: Scope certainty at last — newly scoped companies plan against FY2027 as the first reporting year (reports published 2028).
updates.headline: Omnibus I published in the Official Journal as Directive (EU) 2026/470

updates.detail: SB 253's closest sibling advances: Scope 1/2 from 2028, Scope 3 from 2029, GHG Protocol-based, >$1B revenue threshold, ISSB-report reciprocity. Awaits Assembly action.
updates.so_what: Doing business in NY at >$1B revenue? Pencil in Scope 1/2 for 2028 — Assembly passage still required.
updates.headline: New York Senate passes Climate Corporate Data Accountability Act (S9072A)

updates.detail: Japan phases it in by size: the largest Prime Market companies report for the fiscal year ending March 2027, with smaller tiers following in 2028 and 2029. Among Q1 2026 adoption steps alongside the UK's SRS S1/S2 publication (the FCA consulted on mandatory application from January 1, 2027; that consultation closed March 20, 2026 and a policy statement is expected in autumn 2026) and South Korea's KSDS 1/2 issuance.
updates.so_what: Listed in Japan, the UK, or Korea? Local ISSB-aligned reporting lands FY2027–2028.
updates.headline: Japan mandates ISSB-aligned disclosure, largest listed companies first

updates.detail: The extended consultation (Oct 20, 2025 – Jan 31, 2026) on hourly matching, deliverability, and consequential accounting closes with heavy engagement and sharply divergent views on market-based accounting.
updates.so_what: Keep granular (hourly-capable) electricity data accessible — whichever way the rule lands, granularity wins.
updates.headline: Scope 2 consultation closes: ~1,100 responses from 56 countries

updates.detail: GHGP's first standard for land-sector emissions, biogenic products, and CO2 removals released as final — the first completed deliverable of the revision cycle.
updates.so_what: Agriculture and removals accounting now has final rules — the revision cycle's first finished deliverable.
updates.headline: Land Sector and Removals Standard v1.0 published

updates.detail: Panel probes First Amendment compelled-speech claims against SB 253 and SB 261. No ruling as of August 31, 2026 — the single biggest wildcard for California's regime.
updates.so_what: The ruling could void or cement California's regime — build to comply, watch the docket.
updates.headline: Ninth Circuit hears oral argument in Chamber of Commerce v. Sanchez

updates.detail: Financial obligation accrues on 2026 imports of covered goods (iron/steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, hydrogen, electricity), though certificate purchases start February 2027. Only authorised declarants may import above the 50-tonne threshold.
updates.so_what: EU importers: 2026 imports carry real cost — secure supplier emissions data now.
updates.headline: CBAM definitive regime begins

updates.detail: Eight implementing acts + one delegated act (default values, certificate pricing, verification, registry) plus a proposal to extend CBAM to ~180 downstream iron/steel/aluminium product categories from January 1, 2028.
updates.so_what: Default values and certificate mechanics are set — start supplier data collection for 2026 imports.
updates.headline: Commission issues CBAM rulebook and downstream expansion proposal

updates.detail: Financed-emissions-only relief for Scope 3 Category 15, alternative classification systems beyond GICS, clarified jurisdictional measurement-method relief (including partial-entity), and GWP value relief. Effective January 1, 2027; early application permitted. The GHGP version referenced (2004) is unchanged.
updates.so_what: Plan 2027 filings with the reliefs; financial-sector reporters get Category 15 financed-emissions-only relief.
updates.headline: ISSB issues final Amendments to IFRS S2 GHG disclosures

updates.detail: The deal lands on the Council's line — 1,000 employees + €450m turnover (not Parliament's 1,750) — with permanent limited assurance, the value-chain cap, and CSDDD at 5,000 employees/€1.5bn.
updates.so_what: The 1,000-employee threshold survived — final scope call for your entity list.
updates.headline: Trilogue reaches provisional Omnibus I agreement

updates.detail: Decarbonization pathways for ammonia, methanol, HVCs, nitric acid N2O, non-primary chemicals, fertilizer use-phase N2O, and alternative feedstocks.
updates.so_what: Chemicals companies: sector pathways now exist for target-setting.
updates.headline: SBTi publishes Chemicals Sector Pathways

updates.detail: Provisional proposals: eliminate equity share, financial control as primary approach, operational control retained with revised definition, mandatory Scope 3 at 95% inclusion, and 1% exclusion caps for scopes 1 and 2. Explicitly subject to change.
updates.so_what: Assess your consolidation approach now — equity share is likely disappearing and Scope 3 becoming mandatory.
updates.headline: Corporate Standard Phase 1 Progress Update published (provisional)

updates.detail: 45-day rulemaking package: Scope 1/2 reports proposed due August 10, 2026; 'doing business in California' defined via tax-code gross receipts; fee program from 2026.
updates.so_what: First concrete California deadlines proposed — the shape held through 2026.
updates.headline: CARB publishes formal proposed SB 253/261 regulations

updates.detail: Final advice delivered to the Commission (deadline Nov 30; EFRAG describes submission as December 2025) with revised standards including amended ESRS E1.
updates.so_what: Direction locked: big datapoint cuts, confirmed by 2026 adoption.
updates.headline: EFRAG submits final technical advice on simplified ESRS

updates.detail: A motions panel grants an injunction pending appeal against SB 261's climate-risk reports on First Amendment grounds, suspending the January 1, 2026 deadline — while denying relief against SB 253's emissions reporting.
updates.so_what: Climate-risk report deadline suspended — keep TCFD/ISSB content warm; SB 253 emissions reporting is unaffected.
updates.headline: Ninth Circuit enjoins SB 261 enforcement; SB 253 left intact

updates.detail: After the surprise October 22 plenary rejection of the committee mandate, Parliament adopts a deeper-cutting position (1,750 employees + €450m) by 382–249 — later superseded by the 1,000-employee trilogue deal.
updates.so_what: Superseded by the December trilogue deal.
updates.headline: Parliament adopts revised Omnibus negotiating position

updates.detail: ISO and GHGP formally launch the 'Plan to Harmonize Global Carbon Accounting Standards' at COP30, with recognition from the COP30 Presidency and UN Climate High-Level Champions, spanning corporate, project, and product levels.
updates.so_what: Political weight behind a single global carbon accounting rulebook.
updates.headline: Harmonization plan launched at COP30

updates.detail: TNFD support positions its framework as the basis for the ISSB's nature-related disclosure requirements.
updates.so_what: Nature disclosures will be TNFD-shaped — existing TNFD work carries over.
updates.headline: TNFD backs ISSB's nature workstream

updates.detail: Consultation ran November 6 – December 12, 2025: simpler structure, scope-specific requirements, the new OER recognition mechanism, and greater sector/geography differentiation.
updates.so_what: V2.0's final shape became visible here: category system, OER, scope-specific targets.
updates.headline: Second CNZS V2 consultation draft published

updates.detail: Exxon Mobil v. Sanchez raises First Amendment and NSMIA claims; effectively on hold pending the Ninth Circuit's ruling in the Chamber case.
updates.so_what: A second legal front against California — no change to deadlines.
updates.headline: Exxon Mobil files separate challenge to SB 253/261

updates.detail: Consultation on hourly matching/deliverability, improvements to both methods, and separate consequential-impact reporting; originally closing December 19, later extended to January 31, 2026.
updates.so_what: The market-based accounting fight begins — respond if procurement claims matter to you.
updates.headline: Scope 2 and consequential accounting consultations open

updates.detail: 50-tonne annual de minimis covering all CBAM goods except electricity and hydrogen — exempting ~90% of importers while keeping ~99% of embedded emissions covered. Certificate sales moved to February 2027; in force October 20, 2025.
updates.so_what: Small importers (<50t/yr) exempt; everyone else — certificates start Feb 2027.
updates.headline: CBAM Omnibus Regulation (EU) 2025/2083 adopted

updates.detail: The court keeps petitions in abeyance 'until such time as' the SEC reconsiders the rules via notice-and-comment rulemaking or renews its defense — effectively forcing the rescission path.
updates.so_what: Procedural — the rescission path was confirmed here.
updates.headline: Eighth Circuit holds case until SEC reconsiders or defends

updates.detail: Agreement to harmonize the ISO 14060 family with the GHGP corporate suite and co-develop co-branded standards including a joint product carbon footprint standard. Endorsed publicly by ISSB Chair Emmanuel Faber — the structural event behind everything that followed.
updates.so_what: The structural event: two standard families become one — plan for convergence, not parallel compliance.
updates.headline: ISO and GHG Protocol announce strategic partnership

updates.detail: Full revised suite including amended ESRS E1 with ~57% mandatory datapoint reduction proposed; consultation to September 29, 2025.
updates.so_what: Preview of the datapoint cuts, adopted July 2026.
updates.headline: EFRAG publishes amended ESRS exposure drafts

updates.detail: Covers lending, investment, insurance, and capital markets; requires deforestation-exposure assessment and timelines for ceasing new fossil fuel financing. This July 2027 choice deadline was removed on October 8, 2026; both routes now continue with no end date.
updates.so_what: Superseded: SBTi removed the deadline in October 2026 - financial institutions can use either route indefinitely.
updates.headline: FINZ V1.0 released — first net-zero standard for finance

updates.detail: Guidance on covered entities, revenue definition, and first-cycle expectations ahead of formal rulemaking — CARB having missed its July 1, 2025 statutory rulemaking deadline.
updates.so_what: First official read on who's covered and what year one requires.
updates.headline: CARB issues FAQs on SB 253/261

updates.detail: Phase 1 exposure draft: comprehensive amendments to 9 priority standards and targeted amendments to 41 more; comments closed November 30, 2025.
updates.so_what: Industry metric refresh underway — watch your sector's standard.
updates.headline: ISSB proposes comprehensive review of SASB Standards

updates.detail: Days before the final trilogue (cancelled June 23), the Commission announces intent to withdraw; Council negotiations subsequently collapse. The proposal is dormant, never adopted.
updates.so_what: The Green Claims Directive is blocked, not withdrawn — but EmpCo still bans offset-based neutrality claims from Sep 2026; audit product claims now.
updates.headline: Commission moves to withdraw Green Claims Directive

updates.detail: First 17 jurisdictional profiles published (14 targeting full adoption) plus 16 snapshots, covering Australia, Brazil, Hong Kong, Malaysia, Nigeria, Türkiye, and others.
updates.so_what: The ISSB baseline is the global default — map your exposure by jurisdiction.
updates.headline: IFRS Foundation: 36 jurisdictions adopting or finalizing ISSB adoption

updates.detail: Four proposed reliefs: financed-emissions-only Category 15, GICS flexibility, jurisdictional measurement-method relief, and GWP value relief. Comments closed June 27, 2025.
updates.so_what: Preview of the 2027 reliefs.
updates.headline: ISSB publishes exposure draft of targeted S2 amendments

updates.detail: Directive (EU) 2025/794 delays wave 2 reporting to FY2027 and wave 3 to FY2028 — buying time for the substantive Omnibus negotiation.
updates.so_what: Wave 2/3 breathing room: first reports FY2027/FY2028.
updates.headline: Stop-the-clock directive adopted

updates.detail: The Commission withdraws from defending the 2024 rules in the Eighth Circuit; state intervenors take up the defense.
updates.so_what: The federal rule was effectively finished here — planning pivoted to California and the EU.
updates.headline: SEC votes to stop defending its climate rules

updates.detail: Consultation ran March 18 – June 1, 2025: scope 1/2 split, low-carbon electricity commitment by 2040, scope 3 flexibility options, and BVCM recognition proposals.
updates.so_what: First look at the V2.0 architecture.
updates.headline: First CNZS V2 consultation draft published

updates.detail: The proposal that reshaped EU sustainability reporting: stop-the-clock postponement plus substantive CSRD/CSDDD amendments (1,000-employee threshold), with CBAM simplification in parallel.
updates.so_what: The EU blinked on scope — reporting programs went into re-planning.
updates.headline: Commission publishes the Omnibus I package

updates.detail: No enforcement against entities making good-faith efforts; first-year Scope 1/2 may use data already in the company's possession as of December 5, 2024.
updates.so_what: Year one is good-faith: report with the data you have and document the effort.
updates.headline: CARB issues enforcement-discretion notice for first cycle

updates.detail: Moves CARB's rulemaking deadline to July 1, 2025 (compliance dates unchanged) and allows parent-level consolidated reporting.
updates.so_what: Parent-level consolidated filing allowed — decide your filing entity.
updates.headline: SB 219 signed, amending SB 253/261

updates.detail: Corporate Standard, Scope 2, Scope 3, and AMI TWGs formed from 1,300+ applications — the working machinery of the revision cycle. The Scope 3 TWG alone held 42 meetings through end-2025.
updates.so_what: The people rewriting the rules were seated here — the progress updates that followed trace to these groups.
updates.headline: Four Technical Working Groups announced

updates.detail: New governance for the revision era: a 10-member Steering Committee and the Independent Standards Board, which holds the mandate to review and approve GHGP standards.
updates.so_what: New approval gate (the ISB) for everything that follows.
updates.headline: Inaugural Steering Committee and Independent Standards Board seated

updates.detail: Governance arrangements give the ISSB an observer seat on the GHGP Independent Standards Board and early input into revisions — the mechanism that will mediate any future S2 reference update.
updates.so_what: Insurance that ISSB reporting won't be yanked onto new GHGP rules without consultation.
updates.headline: IFRS Foundation and GHG Protocol sign MoU

updates.detail: Objectives: align with latest science, address scope 3 challenges, integrate continuous improvement, improve interoperability with GHG Protocol and disclosure regimes.
updates.so_what: The V2.0 revision formally scoped.
updates.headline: SBTi releases Terms of Reference for the CNZS major revision

updates.detail: The rules never take effect; original compliance dates (FY2025 for large accelerated filers) are mooted.
updates.so_what: No SEC compliance clock ever started — and it never restarted.
updates.headline: SEC stays its own climate rules pending judicial review

updates.detail: Final rules require material climate-risk disclosure and Scope 1/2 emissions (if material) for large filers; Scope 3 dropped from the proposal. Immediately challenged by nine petitions filed across six circuits (the 2nd, 5th, 6th, 8th, 11th and D.C. Circuits), consolidated in the Eighth Circuit by lottery in March 2024.
updates.so_what: The high-water mark of US federal climate disclosure — never took effect.
updates.headline: SEC adopts climate disclosure rules

updates.detail: First annual periods under the global baseline begin, subject to jurisdictional adoption, with first-year transition reliefs (climate-first, Scope 3 relief).
updates.so_what: The global baseline went live where adopted.
updates.headline: IFRS S1 and S2 become effective

updates.detail: The Climate Corporate Data Accountability Act and climate-risk disclosure law are signed — the first mandatory US corporate GHG reporting regime, statutorily anchored to the GHG Protocol.
updates.so_what: US mandatory GHG reporting was born here — and the GHG Protocol became law in California.
updates.headline: Governor Newsom signs SB 253 and SB 261

updates.detail: Quarterly embedded-emissions reporting for covered imports, running through December 31, 2025 — no financial obligation yet.
updates.so_what: Reporting-only dry run for importers — the cost phase came in 2026.
updates.headline: CBAM transitional reporting phase begins

updates.detail: Twelve sector-agnostic standards adopted, applied from FY2024 by wave 1 companies — the baseline the 2026 revision now simplifies.
updates.so_what: The original 12 standards — now simplified by the 2026 revision.
updates.headline: Commission adopts ESRS Set 1

updates.detail: The inaugural global sustainability disclosure baseline, with IFRS S2 requiring GHG measurement per the GHG Protocol Corporate Standard (2004).
updates.so_what: GHGP 2004 became the global measurement baseline via S2.
updates.headline: ISSB issues IFRS S1 and IFRS S2

updates.detail: Directive (EU) 2022/2464 in force with phased application from FY2024 — the starting point of the EU reporting arc that the Omnibus later reshaped.
updates.so_what: The EU corporate reporting era begins.
updates.headline: CSRD enters into force

updates.detail: Public surveys and a call for proposals open on the Corporate Standard, Scope 2 Guidance, Scope 3 Standard, and market instruments (through March 2023) — the formal start of the revision cycle this tracker follows.
updates.so_what: The starting gun for everything this tracker follows.
updates.headline: GHG Protocol launches corporate suite revision

acronyms.OCC: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
acronyms.VSME: Voluntary Sustainability Reporting Standard for non-listed SMEs
acronyms.CEAOB: Committee of European Auditing Oversight Bodies
acronyms.EmpCo: Empowering Consumers for the Green Transition Directive
acronyms.WBCSD: World Business Council for Sustainable Development

glossary.AMI: 'Actions & Market Instruments' — the GHG Protocol workstream deciding how clean-power contracts, carbon credits, and other climate actions get reported.
glossary.CDP: The nonprofit disclosure platform (formerly Carbon Disclosure Project) where thousands of companies report emissions annually.
glossary.DIS: The stage in ISO's process where a draft standard is put to a formal vote of national member bodies. Passing needs two-thirds approval of participating members with no more than a quarter of votes cast against; failing sends the draft back to committee.
glossary.FCA: Forest Carbon Accounting — the unresolved forestry piece of the GHG Protocol's land rules. (Not the UK's Financial Conduct Authority, also abbreviated FCA.)
glossary.GHG: Greenhouse gas — CO2 plus methane, N2O, and industrial gases, counted together as CO2-equivalents.
glossary.GWP: Global warming potential — the conversion factors that translate different greenhouse gases into CO2-equivalents.
glossary.ISB: Independent Standards Board — the body that approves GHG Protocol standards.
glossary.JWG: Joint Working Group — a combined ISO + GHG Protocol drafting team.
glossary.LSR: Land Sector and Removals — the GHG Protocol standard for land emissions and carbon removals.
glossary.MRV: Monitoring, reporting and verification — compliance-grade rules for proving emissions numbers.
glossary.OAL: California's Office of Administrative Law — the final legal check before a state regulation takes effect.
glossary.OER: 'Ongoing Emissions Responsibility' — SBTi's track for taking responsibility for emissions a company hasn't yet eliminated, e.g. by funding carbon removals. Voluntary recognition for now; V2.0 turns it into a requirement for larger companies after 2035.
glossary.PCF: Product carbon footprint — the emissions of one product across its whole life cycle.
glossary.RFI: Request for Information — an early questionnaire before drafting begins; more preliminary than a consultation.
glossary.SEC: US Securities and Exchange Commission — the federal stock-market regulator.
glossary.TIG: The ISSB's Transition Implementation Group, which discusses how the climate and general sustainability standards should be applied in practice and publishes its conclusions as non-authoritative guidance.
glossary.TWG: Technical Working Group — the expert committees drafting the GHG Protocol revisions.
glossary.CARB: California Air Resources Board — the state agency writing and enforcing California's climate disclosure rules.
glossary.CBAM: The EU's carbon border tax — importers pay for emissions embedded in steel, aluminium, cement, fertiliser, hydrogen, and electricity brought into the EU.
glossary.CNZS: Corporate Net-Zero Standard — SBTi's main rulebook for net-zero targets.
glossary.CSRD: The EU law requiring large companies to publish externally assured sustainability reports.
glossary.ESMA: The EU's securities markets regulator. Among other things it sets the technical rules for how companies file their reports electronically, including whether sustainability disclosures must be tagged so software can read them.
glossary.ESRS: The detailed EU reporting templates CSRD companies must follow; ESRS E1 is the climate one.
glossary.ETS2: The EU's second emissions trading system, covering fuels supplied for buildings, road transport and small industry from 2028. It is separate from the original EU carbon market for power and heavy industry.
glossary.FINZ: Financial Institutions Net-Zero — SBTi's target rules for banks, insurers, and investors.
glossary.FLAG: SBTi's target rules for companies with forest, land, and agriculture emissions.
glossary.GHGP: GHG Protocol — the de facto global rulebook for corporate emissions accounting.
glossary.ISSB: International Sustainability Standards Board — sets the global baseline rules for sustainability information in annual reports: IFRS S1 (all sustainability topics) and IFRS S2 (climate). Countries adopt them into local law.
glossary.PCAF: Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials — the industry methodology for counting financed emissions.
glossary.SASB: Sustainability Accounting Standards Board — industry-specific disclosure metrics, now maintained by the ISSB.
glossary.SBTi: Science Based Targets initiative — the nonprofit that checks whether corporate climate targets are ambitious enough to match climate science.
glossary.TNFD: Taskforce on Nature-related Financial Disclosures — the voluntary framework for reporting nature-related risks.
glossary.VSME: The EU's voluntary reporting standard for smaller companies — the EU's binding cap on what big companies may demand from small suppliers now sits in the VSRS delegated act rather than here.
glossary.VSRS: The EU's voluntary sustainability reporting standard, in force since September 24, 2026. It matters mainly as a ceiling: a company in CSRD scope cannot demand more sustainability information from a smaller value-chain partner than this standard contains.
glossary.XBRL: The machine-readable tagging format regulators use for digital filings - every reported figure carries a code so software can read and compare it.
glossary.CEAOB: The EU body that coordinates national audit regulators and gives the European Commission technical advice on audit and assurance.
glossary.EFRAG: European Financial Reporting Advisory Group — the technical body that drafts the EU's reporting standards.
glossary.EmpCo: The EU's Empowering Consumers Directive — bans vague green claims and offset-based 'carbon neutral' labels from September 2026.
glossary.eGRID: The US Environmental Protection Agency's dataset of average emissions per unit of electricity by US grid region — the usual source for location-based Scope 2 calculations in the US.
glossary.SB 253: California's law requiring large companies doing business there to publicly report their emissions.
glossary.SB 261: California's companion law requiring reports on climate-related financial risks.
glossary.UK SRS: The UK's own endorsed version of the global ISSB sustainability and climate reporting standards. In-scope listed companies must report against them on a comply-or-explain basis for accounting periods beginning on or after January 1, 2027; voluntary for everyone else.
glossary.IFRS S2: The ISSB's climate disclosure standard — what companies must say about climate risk and emissions in investor reports.
glossary.Omnibus: The EU's 2025–26 simplification package that cut the scope and content of its sustainability reporting laws.
glossary.Scope 1: Emissions from things your company burns or leaks directly — vehicles, boilers, refrigerants.
glossary.Scope 2: Emissions from the electricity, heat, steam, or cooling your company buys.
glossary.Scope 3: Everything else up and down the value chain — suppliers, purchased goods, shipping, travel, how customers use your products. Usually the biggest share and the hardest to measure.
glossary.netting: Subtracting credits or clean-power certificates from measured emissions to show one combined number — increasingly disallowed.
glossary.Method 1: One of two market-based reporting approaches the GHG Protocol is weighing for Scope 2. Method 1 would add hourly matching, deliverability and incrementality requirements. Whether it is optional or required is undecided.
glossary.Method 2: The second market-based Scope 2 approach under consideration: it keeps the existing requirements from the 2015 Scope 2 Guidance unchanged. Companies may report under it; whether that stays permissible is undecided.
glossary.ISSA 5000: The international standard setting out how an assurance provider checks a company's sustainability report.
glossary.preemption: The principle that federal law overrides a conflicting state law. Arguing that a state rule is preempted asks a court or a federal regulator to set it aside, rather than to amend it.
glossary.Article 40a: The provision of the EU Accounting Directive that pulls large non-EU parent groups into EU sustainability reporting based on their EU turnover, with the group-level report filed by a designated EU subsidiary or branch on the parent's behalf.
glossary.Category 15: The Scope 3 category covering emissions from investments — the ISSB now lets reporters limit it to banks' and investors' financed emissions.
glossary.Category 16: A proposed new, mostly optional Scope 3 category for emissions a company facilitates without owning or trading the activity — brokerage, underwriting and similar. Most subcategories would be optional, except for oil and gas distributors.
glossary.ISO 14064-1: The international standards body's version of corporate emissions accounting — now merging with the GHG Protocol.
glossary.GHG Protocol: The de facto global rulebook for how companies count greenhouse gas emissions, maintained by two nonprofits (WRI and WBCSD). Nearly every law and framework builds on it.
glossary.equity share: A consolidation approach where you count emissions in proportion to your ownership stake — proposed for elimination.
glossary.market-based: Counting purchased electricity using your contracts and certificates (like renewable energy credits) instead of the local grid average.
glossary.consolidation: The rules deciding which subsidiaries, joint ventures, and facilities count as part of 'your' company's emissions.
glossary.delegated act: EU fine-print legislation adopted by the Commission — becomes law unless Parliament or Council object during a review ('scrutiny') period.
glossary.deliverability: Whether the power plant behind an energy certificate sits on a grid that could physically have delivered that electricity to the buyer. Proposed as a condition for market-based scope 2 claims under Method 1.
glossary.expired target: An SBTi status for a validated target whose target year has passed with no new submission, or whose mandatory five-year review deadline was missed. It attaches to the individual target rather than to the whole company.
glossary.exposure draft: A draft standard published for public comment before being finalized.
glossary.incrementality: Whether a clean-power purchase caused new generation to be built, rather than paying for generation that already existed. Proposed as a condition for market-based scope 2 claims under Method 1.
glossary.location-based: Counting purchased electricity at the average emissions of your local grid, regardless of what contracts you hold.
glossary.carbon removals: Taking CO2 out of the atmosphere — through trees, soil, or technology — as opposed to emitting less.
glossary.hourly matching: A stricter rule proposed in the GHG Protocol Scope 2 revision: clean-power claims would only count if the clean power was generated in the same hour it was used. A companion 'deliverability' proposal would add a same-region test.
glossary.Official Journal: The EU's official gazette. An EU act is not law until it is published there; the publication date is what starts the clock on entry into force.
glossary.synchronous grid: A set of electricity networks physically joined and running in step at the same frequency, so power can flow across the whole of it - for example the continental European grid, or the eastern, western and Texas grids in the United States.
glossary.call for evidence: An open request from a standard-setter for data, studies and practical experience on a topic, used to shape a draft before any text exists — broader and earlier than a public consultation, which asks for comment on an already-written draft.
glossary.comply-or-explain: A rule a company may decline to follow provided it publicly explains why — weaker than a mandate.
glossary.fatal-flaw review: A short, narrowly scoped consultation asking only whether a draft contains serious errors - not an invitation to redraft it.
glossary.financial control: A consolidation approach where you count 100% of emissions from operations you control financially — proposed as the new default.
glossary.limited assurance: A light-touch external check — a reviewer confirms nothing looks wrong. Cheaper and less thorough than a full audit.
glossary.Practice Statement: An IFRS document that helps companies apply a standard without being mandatory itself. Using it is not required to claim compliance with IFRS Standards, though an individual jurisdiction can choose to require it.
glossary.double materiality: The EU principle that companies report both how climate affects them financially and how they affect the climate.
glossary.financed emissions: The share of emissions attributable to a bank's or investor's loans and investments.
glossary.operational control: A consolidation approach where you count 100% of emissions from operations you run day-to-day.
glossary.public consultation: A formal comment period on a draft — the text is not final and can change.
glossary.reasonable assurance: A full audit at the level of a financial audit — much more evidence, much more cost.
glossary.sector specification: A type of SBTi document, introduced in October 2026, that adds to, overrides or modifies parts of the Corporate Net-Zero Standard for a single sector. It is not a standalone standard and, unlike one, does not need Board of Trustees adoption.
glossary.significant category: Under the revised EU rules, a Scope 3 category large enough that it must be reported. Companies identify their significant categories every year and rescreen all fifteen at least every three years.
glossary.Basis for Conclusions: A document a standard-setter publishes to explain the reasoning behind its decisions. SBTi now uses one to issue clarifications of its criteria, which take effect as soon as the document is published rather than waiting for a new version of the standard.
glossary.deliverability region: The area within which a power plant connected to the grid could reasonably be expected to serve electricity use on that same grid. SBTi groups a company's electricity use into pools on this basis and, under a November 2026 proposal, would require the generator behind a contract or certificate to sit in the same wide-area synchronous grid as the site using the power.
glossary.market stability reserve: The EU emissions trading system's automatic supply valve: it withholds allowances from auction when the surplus in circulation is high, releases them when it is low, and permanently cancels allowances held above a set threshold.
glossary.commercial speech: Speech that proposes a commercial transaction or conveys straightforward factual information about a business. US courts give it less First Amendment protection than political or personal speech, so a government can compel it more easily.
glossary.strict scrutiny: The hardest test in US constitutional law. The government must show a rule serves a compelling interest and is narrowly tailored to it. Rules reviewed this way usually fail.
glossary.intermediate scrutiny: A middle test applied to compelled commercial speech in the US. The government must show a substantial interest and a rule that directly advances it without being more extensive than necessary. Easier to satisfy than strict scrutiny.
glossary.severability: Whether the rest of a law can still stand once a court strikes down part of it. If the struck part is severable, the remainder keeps working.
glossary.preliminary injunction: A court order pausing enforcement of a law while a case is still being decided. It is temporary relief, not a final ruling on whether the law is valid.
glossary.pre-ballot review: An internal check of a near-final standard-setting document before it goes out for the formal vote that approves publication.
glossary.COP31: The 31st annual United Nations climate change conference, held in Antalya, Türkiye in November 2026.

matrix.note: Final standard. New target rules for 11,600+ companies; validation opens Feb 1, 2027. Individual criteria can still move before then: the electricity criteria went out for limited public comment on Nov 5, 2026.
matrix.label: SBTi V2.0

matrix.note: Scope 1/2 upheld on appeal Nov 9, 2026 and first reports came due Nov 10. Scope 3 struck down - less work, more open.
matrix.label: California SB 253

matrix.note: Confirmed to happen; Q2 2027 consultation restated at COP31. The biggest long-term rewrite of how every company counts emissions.
matrix.label: GHGP+ISO merger

matrix.note: Live law. Heavy for EU importers of covered goods; irrelevant if you import none. The downstream expansion is now confirmed in active Council negotiation.
matrix.label: EU border tax (CBAM)

matrix.note: In force since Nov 10, 2026, mandatory FY2027. Slimmer but still the heaviest EU lift; the assurance standard is now out for comment.
matrix.label: Revised ESRS

matrix.note: Draft proposals with strong committee support: 95% coverage + data-quality metadata. Big lift if adopted.
matrix.label: Scope 3 revision

matrix.note: One TWG proposal now agreed: hourly matching, not 24/7. Required-or-optional still open; board decides Dec 15, 2026.
matrix.label: Scope 2 debate

matrix.note: Direction (separate statements, no netting) now has a published 84% mandate from 437 responses; the detail — quality criteria, whether statements start optional — is still open. Would change claims and systems.
matrix.label: Market instruments (AMI)

matrix.note: Final, effective Jan 1, 2027. Heavy only if you touch land, agriculture, or removals.
matrix.label: Land & removals (LSR)

matrix.note: Final, effective Jan 1, 2027. Mostly relief — biggest for financial institutions, plus flexibility for anyone whose local rules differ.
matrix.label: ISSB S2 updates

matrix.note: Law, in force since Sep 27, 2026. A contained to-do for marketing and legal — but now a live exposure, not a deadline.
matrix.label: EU green-claims ban

matrix.note: Passed one chamber. If enacted: SB 253-style reporting from 2028 for NY businesses.

matrix.note: Proposed but not adopted, with no date set, and the rules never applied — near-zero operational impact.

horizon.note: GHG Protocol's technical working group has now agreed to put forward a single proposal rather than two competing methods: an improved location-based method plus a market-based method using hourly matching but explicitly not 24/7 certificate matching, with deliverability as plausible physical connection and incrementality recommended rather than required. Three things a reporting team needs are still open: whether market-based reporting is required or optional, the ranking order of the location-based emission-factor hierarchy (votes split evenly), and how contracts signed under the 2015 guidance are treated. The standards board considers the recommendations on December 15, 2026. Illustrative, bracketed phase-in years of 2031, 2033 and 2035 appear in the outcomes document but are not adopted. Note that SBTi may fix the practical rule for target-setters in January 2027, two years before GHG Protocol's own answer.
horizon.title: Renewable-electricity accounting is still unresolved

horizon.note: A federal appeals court struck down SB 253's Scope 3 requirement on November 9, 2026 while upholding Scope 1 and 2, and sent back to the trial court the question of whether the Scope 3 provisions are severable — that is, whether the rest of the law keeps working without them. The law has a severability clause, which usually favours keeping the remainder, and one commentator reads an injunction against all of SB 253 as a remote possibility. But no date is set, no trial-court ruling is expected before 2027, and rehearing or a Supreme Court petition remain available. Separately, California's rulemaking for 2027 and later — reporting timing, assurance and GHG Protocol interoperability — has still never been formally proposed.
horizon.title: Whether California's emissions law still works without Scope 3

horizon.note: GHG Protocol's proposal: report actual emissions and market instruments (certificates, credits) separately — no more blending them into one number. Its Sept 23, 2026 feedback summary shows 84% of 437 respondents support the split, but the draft only opens for comment in 2027 and many asked for the new statements to start optional.
horizon.title: How clean-power contracts and carbon credits get reported may change

horizon.note: The requirement to obtain limited assurance on an EU sustainability statement is settled; the standard your assurance provider will test against is not. The Commission opened a targeted consultation on November 12, 2026, closing January 18, 2027, and secondary coverage reports it asks whether the standard becomes mandatory from 2027, 2028 or later. The draft is reported to build on ISSA 5000, with the EU Taxonomy treated as assurance criteria, procedures for digital tagging, and rules on relying on third-party verification reports. The delegated act is due by July 1, 2027 at the latest — which means it could land in the middle of the first mandatory reporting year, FY2027.
horizon.title: From which year the EU's assurance standard bites — 2027, 2028 or later

horizon.note: ISO's draft net-zero standard (ISO 14060) closed its international ballot on Sept 10, 2026 and has not advanced since. ISO has published no outcome statement, so reports that the draft failed rest on trade coverage rather than an ISO document, and no revision date is published. Until it lands, SBTi's criteria remain the de facto benchmark for what a net-zero claim has to meet.
horizon.title: There is still no agreed international definition of net zero

overview.matrix_intro: How settled each change is vs. how much work it creates. Editorial estimates — hover a dot for reasoning.

heavy_hitters.who: Any company with an approved science-based target, or planning one (11,600+ companies)
heavy_hitters.what: The rules for setting and maintaining net-zero targets have been rewritten. Larger companies face stricter requirements - including outside verification of their emissions numbers. New targets must follow the new rules from February 2028. A proposal published on November 5, 2026 would let clean-power contracts signed before February 1, 2027 keep their eligibility under the old geography rules, while new ones must meet a tighter same-grid test.
heavy_hitters.title: New rulebook for climate targets — SBTi V2.0 is final
heavy_hitters.action: Check which tier your company falls into, decide whether to submit under the old or new rulebook before the old one closes (Jan 31, 2028), and get any power purchase agreement or certificate contract you are negotiating fully executed before February 1, 2027.

heavy_hitters.who: Companies reporting under ISSB-based rules (in use in 45+ jurisdictions — Japan, UK, Australia…)
heavy_hitters.what: A package of simplifications takes effect: banks and investors only have to count the emissions of their loans and investments (not every financial product), and companies get flexibility where local law conflicts with the default method.
heavy_hitters.title: Global climate disclosure gets easier — updates effective Jan 1, 2027
heavy_hitters.action: Plan 2027 filings with the simplifications — using them early is allowed.

heavy_hitters.who: Effectively everyone — nearly all emissions inventories follow the GHG Protocol, ISO 14064-1, or both
heavy_hitters.what: GHG Protocol and ISO are combining their corporate standards into one. Public comment is planned for Q2 2027; the final version is estimated for late 2028. Core counting rules will change — including which subsidiaries count as 'yours' and whether supply-chain emissions are mandatory.
heavy_hitters.title: The world's two carbon accounting rulebooks are merging
heavy_hitters.action: No rewrite needed yet — but review how your inventory would hold up under the proposed changes before the comment period opens.

heavy_hitters.who: Companies with agriculture, bioenergy, or land in their supply chain — or buying carbon removals
heavy_hitters.what: The GHG Protocol published its first standard for counting land-related emissions and CO2 removals. If your business touches farmland or you plan to count removals toward targets, this is now the rulebook. (Forestry is still being worked out.)
heavy_hitters.title: First-ever rules for land and carbon-removal accounting — in force Jan 1, 2027
heavy_hitters.action: Screen whether any part of your business or supply chain is covered — before the January effective date.

heavy_hitters.who: Anyone importing steel, aluminium, cement, fertiliser, hydrogen, or electricity into the EU
heavy_hitters.what: Since January 2026, covered imports carry a carbon cost under CBAM. Payments begin February 2027, first bill due September 2027 — and a proposal to extend coverage to finished metal products from 2028 is in negotiation, with the final product list not yet fixed.
heavy_hitters.title: The EU's carbon border tax is now real money
heavy_hitters.action: Collect emissions data from your suppliers now — without it, you pay default rates that are usually higher.

heavy_hitters.who: Companies with significant EU business: over 1,000 employees and €450m turnover (non-EU parents have a separate EU-turnover test)
heavy_hitters.what: The EU cut its required reporting datapoints by roughly 60% and took an estimated 80–90% of companies out of scope entirely. The revised standards became law on Sept 21, 2026 and enter into force Nov 10, 2026, mandatory for financial years starting in 2027. For a financial year starting in 2026 you may choose the new standards or the old ones with reliefs — but you have to say which you used. The standards entered into force on November 10, 2026 with no official communication marking it and no implementation guidance issued. Separately, the Commission has now opened consultation on the EU limited assurance standard — the rules your assurance provider will actually test against — closing January 18, 2027, with the mandatory start year (2027, 2028 or later) in play.
heavy_hitters.title: EU sustainability reporting is slimmer — and mandatory from FY2027
heavy_hitters.action: Confirm whether you're still in scope, re-plan reporting against the slimmed template, and get your assurance provider's read on the draft assurance standard in time to respond by January 18, 2027.

heavy_hitters.who: Companies with over $1B revenue doing business in California — including US subsidiaries of non-US groups
heavy_hitters.what: The first mandatory US corporate emissions reports came due on November 10, 2026, and the day before a federal appeals court upheld the Scope 1 and Scope 2 duty while striking down the Scope 3 requirement and the separate climate-risk law. California has published nothing since the deadline. Fee notices begin December 10, 2026 and are payable within 60 days. Whether the rest of the law survives without Scope 3 now sits with the trial court.
heavy_hitters.title: California emissions reporting — Scope 1/2 upheld, Scope 3 struck down
heavy_hitters.action: Keep your Scope 1/2 filing evidence and budget for the December fee notice; stop spending on a California Scope 3 filing and on climate-risk reports, but keep the underlying value-chain data for the EU, ISSB and SBTi regimes.

crosswalk.intro: Corporate emissions reporting is a stack, not a menu. Measurement standards (GHG Protocol, ISO) define how to count; target frameworks (SBTi) define what counts as aligned; disclosure baselines (ISSB) and regulations (EU, California) define who must report what, and they almost all point back at the GHG Protocol. That is why one revision cycle propagates everywhere.

relationships.note: The GHGP Corporate Standard, Scope 2 Guidance, Scope 3 Standard, AMI, and ISO 14064-1 become one co-branded standard (consultation Q2 2027, publication est. Q4 2028). Product (ISO 14067 + GHGP Product Standard) and project standards are being harmonized in parallel.
relationships.title: GHGP + ISO are merging their corporate standards
bullets: One co-branded standard replaces the GHGP corporate suite + ISO 14064-1
Part 1 covers general requirements and the physical GHG inventory; Part 2 covers actions and market instruments, plus guidance documents
Consultation Q2 2027 → publication est. Q4 2028; product & project standards harmonizing in parallel

relationships.note: S2 requires Scopes 1–3 measured per the GHGP Corporate Standard (2004), unless a jurisdiction or exchange mandates a different method — a relief the Dec 2025 amendments extend. The ISSB holds an observer seat on the GHGP standards board; any switch to the revised GHGP standard requires an ISSB exposure draft and public consultation — reporters are not automatically moved.
relationships.title: IFRS S2 hard-wires the GHG Protocol
bullets: S2 requires Scopes 1–3 per the GHGP Corporate Standard (2004) — today's version, not the revision
ISSB holds an observer seat on the GHGP standards board
Moving S2 to the revised standard requires an exposure draft + consultation — no automatic migration

relationships.note: SB 253 statutorily requires GHG Protocol conformance, and CARB has pinned reporting to current versions — stating it 'will not dynamically update to reflect GHG Protocol developments.' Revised GHGP standards would need a new rulemaking, creating a likely lag and possible divergence. New York's Senate-passed bill takes the opposite route: it references the GHG Protocol standards generically, names no edition, and lets the state adopt an alternative standard from 2034.
relationships.title: California pins SB 253 to specific GHGP versions
bullets: SB 253 writes GHGP conformance into statute; CARB pinned specific versions
CARB: reporting “will not dynamically update to reflect GHG Protocol developments”
Revised GHGP → new rulemaking needed → lag + dual-methodology risk; NY's bill, by contrast, names no edition

relationships.note: Revised ESRS E1 requires Scope 1, Scope 2 (location- and market-based) and Scope 3 by significant category, and directs undertakings to consider the GHG Protocol Corporate Standard (2004), with Commission Recommendation (EU) 2021/2279 or EN ISO 14064-1:2018 as references they may also consider. ESRS requirements take precedence over all three. EFRAG tracks GHGP revisions for future alignment.
relationships.title: ESRS E1 builds on GHGP with ISO as alternative
bullets: E1 requires Scope 1, Scope 2 (both methods), and Scope 3 consistent with GHGP standards
Commission Recommendation (EU) 2021/2279 and EN ISO 14064-1:2018 may also be considered; ESRS requirements take precedence over all three
The revised 2026 ESRS keeps this architecture; EFRAG tracks GHGP revisions

relationships.note: SBTi target boundaries, progress measurement, and assurance all consume GHGP-based inventories. V2.0 was finalized mid-revision, so SBTi plans its own provisional accounting guidance while the GHGP revision runs (preliminary guidance expected Q4 2026 for consultation and testing). V2.0's location-based scope 2 basis and hourly provisions anticipate the GHGP Scope 2 direction — but GHGP's Scope 2 outcome is still open, a real divergence risk.
relationships.title: SBTi targets sit on GHGP inventories
bullets: Target boundaries, progress, and assurance all consume GHGP-based inventories
V2.0 finalized mid-revision → SBTi plans its own provisional accounting guidance (preliminary ~Q4 2026)
V2.0 anticipates GHGP's Scope 2 direction — but that outcome is still open: divergence risk

relationships.note: SBTi's FLAG Standard revision (call for input open) will clarify its alignment with the LSR Standard/Guidance that becomes effective January 1, 2027 — a direct methodological coupling on land and removals.
relationships.title: FLAG V2 will align with GHGP Land Sector & Removals
bullets: FLAG revision will harmonize with the GHGP LSR Standard/Guidance
LSR effective Jan 1, 2027 · FLAG evidence due Oct 8, 2026
Land-exposed companies get one coupled accounting + target system

relationships.note: The simplified E1 was drafted for interoperability with IFRS S2, so companies reporting under both regimes can run one climate dataset. New York's bill even offers ISSB-report reciprocity.
relationships.title: Revised ESRS deepens ISSB interoperability
bullets: Simplified E1 drafted for interoperability with IFRS S2
One climate dataset can serve both regimes
New York's bill even offers ISSB-report reciprocity

relationships.note: CBAM prices product-level embedded emissions calculated with installation-level, EU ETS-aligned MRV rules — not GHGP corporate inventories. Companies in scope run parallel datasets: a GHGP/ESRS corporate inventory and supplier-specific installation data for imports. The ISO–GHGP product standard harmonization may eventually narrow this gap.
relationships.title: CBAM does NOT use corporate inventories
bullets: CBAM prices product-level embedded emissions via EU ETS-aligned installation MRV
In-scope importers run parallel datasets: corporate GHGP/ESRS + supplier installation data
ISO–GHGP product standard harmonization may narrow the gap later

relationships.note: The SEC has proposed rescinding its climate rule with no replacement, while ISSB adoption spreads (Japan, the UK, Australia among the 45+ jurisdictions that have adopted the standards or are taking steps to introduce them) and California proceeds. US multinationals face the baseline anyway — through the EU (the Article 40a standard for non-EU groups from FY2028), ISSB-adopting jurisdictions, and state law.
relationships.title: US federal exits while states and the baseline advance
bullets: SEC proposes to exit with no replacement; the ISSB baseline keeps spreading (Japan, UK, Australia…)
California proceeds — first reports Nov 2026
US multinationals meet the baseline anyway: EU Art. 40a (non-EU groups, FY2028), ISSB jurisdictions, state law

relationships.note: GHGP's AMI direction — separate statements for physical inventory, market-based instruments, and action impacts, with no netting — would change how renewable procurement, certificates, and 'impact' claims are reported and how SBTi recognizes them. SBTi says it is coordinating on multi-statement structures; EmpCo's ban on offset-based neutrality claims (Sept 2026) pushes the same direction in the EU.
relationships.title: Multi-statement reporting could reshape claims everywhere
bullets: AMI direction: separate statements for inventory, market instruments, and action impacts — no netting
Would reshape renewable procurement claims and how SBTi recognizes instruments
EmpCo's offset-claim ban (Sep 2026) pushes the same way in the EU

divergence_watchlist.title: Frozen vs. moving GHGP versions
divergence_watchlist.detail: California (and IFRS S2, for now) reference the current GHGP standards while GHGP revises them. If regulators lag the Q4 2028 consolidated standard, companies may have to maintain dual inventories — one per the frozen version, one per the new standard.
bullets: California + IFRS S2 reference current GHGP versions while GHGP rewrites them
If regulators lag the Q4 2028 standard → companies maintain dual inventories

divergence_watchlist.title: Scope 2 accounting outcome
divergence_watchlist.detail: GHGP's Scope 2 consultation showed deep divergence (hourly matching vs. status quo vs. multiple approaches). SBTi V2.0 already anchors targets to location-based inventories and requires hourly-interval disclosure from large electricity users. If GHGP lands elsewhere, target accounting and inventory accounting could split.
bullets: GHGP consultation split (hourly matching vs. status quo vs. multiple approaches); reported support for hourly matching just ~22%
SBTi V2.0 already uses location-based accounting + hourly disclosure for large users — if GHGP lands elsewhere, target and inventory accounting split

divergence_watchlist.title: Scope 3 boundaries
divergence_watchlist.detail: GHGP proposes 95% inclusion with data-type disaggregation and a possible Category 16; California proposes only five mandatory Scope 3 categories; SBTi V2.0 uses a ≥5%-significance boundary; the revised ESRS requires only significant Scope 3 categories, with a full 15-category screen at least every three years. Four different Scope 3 boundaries for the same value chain.
bullets: GHGP: 95% inclusion + possible Cat. 16 · California: 5 mandatory categories · SBTi: ≥5% significance · ESRS: significant categories only
Four different Scope 3 boundaries for the same value chain

divergence_watchlist.title: Litigation risk in the US
divergence_watchlist.detail: The Ninth Circuit's pending merits ruling on SB 253/261 could reshape state authority to mandate climate disclosure; SB 261 is already enjoined pending appeal and CARB is not enforcing it, while SB 253 was expressly left to proceed — and with it, the only mandatory US corporate reporting regime.
bullets: Ninth Circuit merits ruling (argued Jan 9, 2026) still pending
Could reshape state authority to mandate climate disclosure — and the only mandatory US corporate regime

landscape.intro: Corporate emissions rules come in three layers, and companies usually face all three at once. Right now, every layer is being rewritten — which is why this dashboard exists.
landscape.footer: The layers connect: disclosure laws and target frameworks almost all point back at the GHG Protocol for the actual counting — the full map is in How they relate.

frameworks.description: The GHG Protocol Corporate Standard (2004), Scope 2 Guidance (2015), and Scope 3 Standard (2011) are the measurement backbone for nearly every corporate emissions inventory worldwide. All three are being revised simultaneously through Technical Working Groups, and will be consolidated with ISO 14064-1 into a single co-branded corporate standard.

workstreams.summary: On July 29, 2026, GHG Protocol and ISO announced they will combine their corporate carbon accounting standards into a single co-branded global standard, integrating the GHGP Corporate Standard, Scope 2 Guidance, Scope 3 Standard, the Actions & Market Instruments workstream, and ISO 14064-1. The deliverable is structured as Part 1 (General Requirements and Physical GHG Inventory) and Part 2 (Actions and Market Instruments).

confidence.reasoning: Announced in an official GHGP press release, FAQ, and published Standard Development Plan (all dated July 29, 2026). The decision to consolidate and the approval structure are final; the title, the two-part structure and the timeline are all still marked draft or estimated. On the dates specifically: Q2 2027 was restated in the week by both organisations' representatives at COP31, as reported by a trade association rather than published by either body, and the Scope 2 workshop outcomes independently give Q2 2027 for the combined draft's consultation. The Q4 2028 publication quarter was NOT restated — the same COP31 report says only "publication in 2028" — so the quarter remains a published plan of July 2026.

workstreams.summary: The 2015 Scope 2 Guidance is being revised inside the consolidated corporate standard. A public consultation closed January 31, 2026 and GHG Protocol published a two-method direction of travel on October 16, 2026: one method adding hourly matching, deliverability and incrementality, one keeping the 2015 rules. A technical working group workshop held October 20-22, 2026 in Washington DC, whose outcomes were published with a newest document dated November 10, 2026, moved this on materially. The group will put forward a single proposal rather than competing alternatives, with an improved location-based method built on a ranked emission-factor hierarchy and a market-based method using hourly matching but explicitly not 24/7 certificate matching. Several questions a reporting team would ask are still open: whether market-based reporting is required or optional, the ranking order of the location-based hierarchy, and how long-term contracts signed under the 2015 guidance are treated. All documents are marked draft and subject to change, and the outcomes are described as an interim step towards a final standard that still requires public consultation.

confidence.reasoning: Held at medium, and the November 10 workshop outcomes support that rating rather than lifting it. The direction is now documented in far more detail than a month ago — a single proposal, hourly matching without 24/7 matching, deliverability as plausible physical connection, incrementality recommended but not required — and an informal poll recorded 22 members able to support a single proposal with none opposed. But the documents are explicitly draft and subject to change and are called an interim step requiring public consultation; the ranking order of the location-based emission-factor hierarchy is unresolved with votes split evenly; whether market-based reporting is required or optional is open; the treatment of contracts signed under the 2015 guidance is undecided; and "Standard Supply Service" is recorded as unresolved with no direction indicated. The phase-in dates that appear in the outcomes are bracketed and illustrative, not adopted. Written alternatives can still go to the standards board, which does not consider the secretariat's recommendations until December 15, 2026 — so the design could still change before anything is settled.

key_points: The TWG will develop a single proposal rather than competing alternatives — an informal poll recorded 22 members able to support one, with none opposed; written alternatives can still go to the standards board
The proposed market-based method uses hourly matching but explicitly NOT 24/7 certificate matching, with deliverability defined as a plausible physical connection

Incrementality is recommended but not required — though companies would have to disclose their incremental share, qualifying through either a long-term offtake contract or an asset-age limit (around 15 years was discussed)
Still open, and the question that matters most: whether market-based reporting is required or optional. Reporting would be optional below a size or load threshold (broadly supported)
Still open: the ranking order of the location-based emission-factor hierarchy (most recent data first, or closest geographic match first) — votes were split evenly
Still undecided: how long-term clean-power contracts signed under the 2015 guidance would be treated

Illustrative only, NOT adopted: the outcomes document brackets a phase-in of 2031, 2033 and 2035 for the largest, middle and smaller load tiers, with the 2015 Guidance remaining available until roughly 2035-2039
Decision calendar: subgroup recommendations November 23-24, 2026; materials to the standards board December 1; board considers the secretariat's recommendations December 15, 2026

The outcomes are published only in the standards-development repository — the Scope 2 Guidance workstream page does not mention the workshop or link the documents

confidence.reasoning: The Scope 1 and Scope 2 duty is now the most settled part of this workstream: a published appellate opinion of November 9, 2026 affirmed the denial of an injunction against it, the regulation setting the deadline is in force, and the deadline passed on November 10 with the obligation intact. Held at medium rather than higher for three reasons. First, the same ruling struck down the Scope 3 requirement and remanded severability to the district court, so the shape of the regime from 2027 is genuinely unsettled — one commentator reading the ruling does not expect a trial-court decision before 2027. Second, the ruling is preliminary-injunction relief, not a final merits judgment, and rehearing, en banc review and a petition to the Supreme Court all remain available; the challengers' other, non-speech claims are still pending. Third, the 2027-and-later requirements most reporting teams must plan against sit in a rulemaking for which no 45-day notice has been issued. A separate non-judicial route remains open: the OCC's October 29, 2026 request that California exempt federally chartered banks is published (news release 2026-95, a correction to last week's record, which marked it unpublished), CARB has published no response, and the OCC has taken no further action through news release 2026-100 of November 13, 2026.

workstreams.summary: SB 261's climate-related financial risk reports (companies >$500M revenue) were due January 1, 2026, but a Ninth Circuit panel enjoined enforcement on November 18, 2025 on First Amendment grounds. On November 9, 2026 the same court decided the appeal and reversed as to SB 261: it held the law does not regulate commercial speech, applied strict scrutiny, and found that compelling companies to produce subjective, politically contested assessments of climate risk fails that test, noting that the state all but concedes it cannot satisfy it. The case returns to the district court for preliminary relief consistent with the mandate. One judge would have gone further and enjoined SB 253 as well. There is no reporting obligation while this stands, and CARB has set no replacement deadline.

confidence.reasoning: The near-term position is now much better supported than a week ago: a published appellate opinion of November 9, 2026 holds that SB 261 fails strict scrutiny and reverses the denial of preliminary relief, so there is no reporting obligation and none is in prospect. The rating is nonetheless held at medium rather than raised, because what issued is a ruling on preliminary relief rather than a final merits judgment, and a contrary outcome remains procedurally available: rehearing, en banc review and a petition to the Supreme Court have not been exhausted, no mandate-issuance date is published, and the district court has yet to enter relief on remand. The dashboard's own rule is not to rate above medium while a court could still flip the outcome. What has changed is the direction and the reasoning, not the certainty: a reader should now plan on SB 261 not applying, where a week ago the honest answer was that nobody knew.

workstreams.summary: New York's Climate Corporate Data Accountability Act (S9072A) passed the state Senate February 10, 2026 and awaits Assembly action. It mirrors SB 253 — GHG Protocol-based, >$1B revenue, Scope 1/2 from 2028, Scope 3 from 2029 — and adds ISSB-report reciprocity. New Jersey's reintroduced bill (S679) was amended in committee to drop Scope 3. Illinois, Colorado, and Washington bills stalled in 2025 and have not been revived.
